title.zh: 给 AI Agent 用的专属基础设施
title.en: Agent-Native Infrastructure (Built for Machines, Not Humans)

old_assumption.zh: 邮箱、浏览器、支付和身份验证都是围绕人类图形界面（GUI）设计的。
old_assumption.en: Email, browsers, payments, and auth are designed around human GUIs.

new_shift.zh: AI Agent 正在成为软件的新一类用户，它们不需要好看的 UI，需要的是极简 API、沙盒与独立身份。
new_shift.en: AI agents are becoming primary software users—they need headless APIs, sandboxes, and machine identities, not pretty dashboards.

zh: 列出 5 个目前完全为人类设计的互联网基础设施（如邮箱、日历、支付、客服），分析当使用者变成 AI Agent 时，原产品的最大摩擦点是什么，以及对应的极简 API 替代品该如何设计。
在 [你的技术栈/熟悉领域] 中，如果要为一个自主运行的 AI Agent 提供安全沙盒和权限审计层，最小的独立开发者 MVP 应该只做哪 3 个核心接口？
en: List 5 internet primitives built for humans (email, calendar, payments, auth) and explain what breaks when the user is an AI agent—plus how a headless API replacement should work.
In [Your Tech Stack/Domain], what are the 3 minimal endpoints needed to build an indie-friendly sandbox and permission layer for autonomous AI agents?

note.zh: 专为 AI Agent 设计的邮箱 API 基础设施
note.en: Email inbox API built specifically for AI agents

note.zh: 为 AI 生成代码提供安全隔离的云端代码沙盒
note.en: Open-source cloud sandboxes for AI-executed code

title.zh: 用完即弃的“一次性定制微软件”
title.en: Disposable, Single-Use Personal Software

old_assumption.zh: 写软件成本极高，所以每个程序都必须做成通用产品、长期维护并服务成千上万人。
old_assumption.en: Software is expensive to build, so every app must be generalized, maintained for years, and built for thousands.

new_shift.zh: 代码生成成本趋近于零后，为一次旅行、一次搬家或一次数据清洗花 10 分钟生成专属本地网页应用变得完全划算。
new_shift.en: With near-zero code generation cost, spinning up a bespoke local app for one trip, one move, or one dataset is now completely practical.

zh: 我最近需要处理一件一次性但很繁琐的事：[描述你的具体任务]。请帮我设计一个单文件 HTML/JS 本地微工具的极简规格，让我 10 分钟内生成并用完即弃。
盘点 [你的职业/生活场景] 中，哪些原本只能凑合用 Excel 做的临时任务，现在更适合用“一次性定制小网页”彻底解决？
en: I have a tedious one-off task: [Describe Your Task]. Spec out a single-file local HTML/JS micro-app I can generate in 10 minutes, use once, and discard.
In [Your Role/Life Context], which messy tasks people currently hack together in spreadsheets are better solved by disposable, bespoke single-use web apps?

note.zh: “家常软件”概念：只为自己和家人做的小程序
note.en: The classic essay on apps cooked just for yourself and loved ones

title.zh: 本地优先 + 端侧小模型的反云端软件
title.en: Local-First Software Powered by Tiny Edge Models

old_assumption.zh: 智能应用必须把用户数据传到云端、调用昂贵的大模型 API 并收取月度订阅费。
old_assumption.en: Smart apps must upload user data to the cloud, pay cloud LLM APIs, and charge monthly subscriptions.

new_shift.zh: 轻量级端侧视觉/语音/文本模型已经小到能在普通笔记本离线流畅运行，隐私敏感场景迎来“零 API 成本”的一次性买断新机会。
new_shift.en: Tiny open vision/audio/text models now run offline on consumer laptops, unlocking privacy-first, zero-API-cost software.

zh: 列出 5 个用户极度在意隐私、不敢上传云端的 [某领域，如医疗/财务/个人日记] 场景，设计一个完全离线运行、结合端侧小模型的本地优先工具。
对比云端大模型 API 与本地小模型（如 Whisper/Moondream/Qwen 小参数版），在 [具体使用场景] 中，如何通过任务拆解让端侧小模型达到 90% 的可用效果？
en: List 5 privacy-sensitive workflows in [Domain, e.g., finance/health/journaling] where users refuse cloud uploads, and design an offline local-first tool using tiny edge models.
For [Specific Use Case], how can I decompose the task so a small local model (Whisper/Moondream/small LLM) hits 90% accuracy with zero cloud API cost?

note.zh: 极致轻量的开源端侧视觉理解模型，可本地离线运行
note.en: Tiny open-source vision model built to run anywhere on-device

note.zh: Ink & Switch 提出的本地优先软件架构宣言
note.en: Ink & Switch's foundational essay on local-first architecture

title.zh: 无界面 / 隐形自动化（Zero-UI Automation）
title.en: Zero-UI Ambient Automation

old_assumption.zh: 好工具必须有精美的控制台和仪表盘，让用户每天点开操作。
old_assumption.en: Good tools need polished dashboards that you open and operate every day.

new_shift.zh: 最高级的个人工具根本没有界面——它藏在快捷键、文件夹监听或后台脚本里，平时完全隐身，只在异常时才提醒你。
new_shift.en: The best personal tools have no UI at all—they live in hotkeys, folder watchers, and background scripts, staying invisible until an exception needs you.

zh: 盘点我每天在电脑上重复超过 3 次的机械操作：[列出 2-3 个具体动作]。帮我把它们改造成“零界面后台自动化”（如文件夹监听、全局快捷键、定时脚本），并给出最小实现方案。
如果把 [你常用的某个效率工具/流程] 的图形界面全部砍掉，只保留“触发条件 → 自动执行 → 异常通知”三步，它的极简工作流应该怎么设计？
en: Audit these repetitive computer actions I do 3+ times a day: [List 2-3 Actions]. Redesign them as zero-UI background automations (folder watchers, hotkeys, cron scripts) with a minimal implementation plan.
If you stripped the entire GUI from [Workflow/Tool You Use] and kept only 'trigger -> silent execution -> exception alert', what would the minimal pipeline look like?

note.zh: macOS 经典无界面文件自动化工具，规则配好后几乎无需再打开
note.en: Classic macOS ambient file automation that runs silently once configured

note.zh: 用全局快捷键触发任意本地脚本，把重型操作压缩成 1 秒肌肉记忆
note.en: Trigger local scripts via global hotkeys, turning heavy workflows into 1-second muscle memory

title.zh: 用私人脚本给大厂网页打“外挂补丁”
title.en: Patching Annoying Web Apps with Personal Userscripts

old_assumption.zh: 每天高频使用的网站难用、信息杂乱或少个导出按钮，只能忍着等官方更新。
old_assumption.en: If a web app you use daily has cluttered UI or lacks an export button, you just have to live with it.

new_shift.zh: AI 写浏览器脚本的成本趋近于零，任何人都能花 5 分钟在本地隐藏噪音、注入快捷键或一键导出数据，把别人的软件改成自己的形状。
new_shift.en: AI makes writing userscripts and tiny browser extensions effortless—spend 5 minutes to hide noise, add hotkeys, or inject export buttons into any site you use.

zh: 我每天都要用 [某个网站/Web 系统]，但它最让我烦躁的 2 个问题是：[描述痛点，如侧边栏太吵/缺少一键复制/翻页麻烦]。请帮我写一个极简 Tampermonkey 油猴脚本，直接在本地修复这些体验。
列出 5 个你在 [某高频网站，如 GitHub/B站/Notion/邮箱] 上最值得用 50 行 JS 脚本改造的“反人性交互”，并按提效幅度排序。
en: I use [Specific Website/Web App] every day, and two things drive me crazy: [List Friction Points]. Write a minimal Tampermonkey userscript to patch these locally.
List 5 high-leverage micro-patches (under 50 lines of JS each) that dramatically improve daily usability on [Frequent Site, e.g., GitHub/Gmail/YouTube].

note.zh: “可塑软件”理念：用户应当能像改造房间一样自由微调自己使用的软件
note.en: The vision that users should be able to reshape the software they use to fit their own needs

title.zh: 把个人生活数据当作“私有上下文 API”来运维
title.en: Treating Personal Life Data as a Private Context API

old_assumption.zh: 笔记、账单、阅读、健康记录散落在十几个商业 App 里，想复盘只能人工来回翻。
old_assumption.en: Notes, expenses, reading logs, and health data stay trapped across a dozen separate commercial apps.

new_shift.zh: 借鉴企业数据中台思路，把个人高频数据定期沉淀到本地纯文本或 SQLite，让任何 AI 随时能安全读取你的“个人上下文”来辅助决策。
new_shift.en: Borrowing from enterprise data pipelines, syncing your key personal records into local Markdown or SQLite lets any AI reason over your real life context privately.

zh: 我想把目前分散在 [列出你常用的 3 个 App，如微信读书/记账软件/Apple Health] 的个人数据，定期同步到本地纯文本/SQLite 形成我的“私有上下文库”。请帮我设计一个极简、低维护的目录结构与同步方案。
如果我把过去半年的 [某类个人记录，如消费/日程/学习笔记] 整理成结构化文本喂给 AI，请设计 5 个平时我自己绝对看不出来的“跨维度复盘提问”。
en: I want to sync my scattered data from [List 3 Apps, e.g., Kindle/Expense Tracker/Calendar] into a local Markdown/SQLite personal context store. Design a minimal, low-maintenance folder structure and sync workflow.
Once I feed 6 months of structured [Type of Personal Log] to an AI, give me 5 cross-dimensional review prompts that reveal patterns I would never spot manually.

note.zh: 开源个人数据聚合接口，将个人各类数字足迹统一变成可编程本地数据
note.en: Open-source Python interface unifying personal digital footprints into programmable local data

title.zh: 把非结构化文档当作“源码”编译成结构化系统
title.en: Treating Unstructured Docs as Source Code Compiled into Systems

old_assumption.zh: 长文档、会议纪要、PDF 规则书和邮件只能写给人看，改了之后靠人工通知同步。
old_assumption.en: Specs, memos, PDFs, and emails are static text for humans—changes stay synced by manual reminders.

new_shift.zh: 把自然语言规则/文档当成“源码”，用 AI 流水线自动编译成 JSON 配置、测试断言、任务清单或日程变更，文档改了系统自动跟着变。
new_shift.en: Treat prose specs and notes as source code that compiles via LLM pipelines into JSON rules, test assertions, tasks, or calendar updates.

zh: 我有一类经常更新的文本/规则文档：[描述文档类型，如项目需求/报销规则/读书笔记]。请帮我设计一个“文档 → 结构化数据/任务清单”的自动提取与校验流水线。
在 [你的个人或团队工作流] 中，哪些“改了文档却忘了改配置/代码/待办”的同步断层，最适合用轻量脚本 + AI 校验来消除？
en: I maintain frequently updated prose docs like [Spec/Policy/Notes]. Design a pipeline that compiles them into structured JSON, checklists, or test rules with drift checks.
In [Your Workflow], where do docs and downstream configs/tasks drift out of sync, and how can a lightweight script + LLM check keep them aligned?

note.zh: 用结构化 Schema 约束大模型输出，让文本能稳定驱动下游工具
note.en: Constrained structured outputs turn natural language into reliable downstream program inputs

title.zh: 给危险或高成本动作加一层“本地沙盒预演”
title.en: Adding a Local Dry-Run Sandbox Before High-Stakes Actions

old_assumption.zh: 批量改文件、群发消息、调外部接口或跑自动化脚本，要么小心翼翼手动点，要么出事了才后悔。
old_assumption.en: Batch file edits, bulk sends, or automation scripts either get clicked painfully by hand or break things in production.

new_shift.zh: 先在本地临时目录或“只打印计划不执行（Dry-Run）”模式下跑一遍预览与差异对比，确认无误再放行，极大降低自动化焦虑。
new_shift.en: Running a dry-run preview with clear diffs in a temp folder before real execution removes the fear of automation mistakes.

zh: 我打算写一个自动处理 [文件整理/数据清洗/批量修改] 的脚本，最怕误删或改错。请帮我设计标准的 `--dry-run` 预览与备份回滚机制。
盘点我最容易“手滑点错或批量改崩”的 3 个电脑操作，如何用极简的预演/确认步骤把容错率拉满？
en: I'm automating [File Cleanup/Data Transform/Batch Edit] and fear accidental data loss. Design a clean `--dry-run` diff preview and rollback safety net.
List 3 computer tasks where a slip-up hurts most, and add a fast preview/confirmation guard that keeps speed high and risk low.

note.zh: 隔离工作区与预演机制是工程界对抗“改坏现状”最朴素也最可靠的护栏
note.en: Isolated workspaces and dry-run previews are simple, battle-tested guards against unintended changes

title.zh: 用“声明式配置/脚本”替代靠记忆点 20 步界面
title.en: Replacing 20-Click Menus with Declarative Configs & Scripts

old_assumption.zh: 换电脑、重装环境或改一套配置，只能凭印象在设置面板里一步步点回去。
old_assumption.en: Setting up a new machine or tweaking a workflow means clicking through 20 menu screens from memory.

new_shift.zh: 把偏好、环境依赖和常用组合写成一份可读的配置文件或脚本，重装、迁移和分享都能一键复现，再也不怕忘掉当初怎么配出来的。
new_shift.en: Capturing preferences, setups, and shortcuts in declarative configs or scripts makes new machines, rollbacks, and sharing reproducible in seconds.

zh: 列出我每次换设备或重装时最容易漏掉的 5 个环境/工具配置项：[填入你的常用环境或工具]。帮我设计一份可版本管理的极简配置清单或一键初始化脚本思路。
在 [你日常使用的某个软件/工作流] 中，哪些“靠手动勾选、记笔记”的设置其实可以沉淀成模板或配置，省去重复劳动？
en: List 5 setup items I easily forget when switching machines or environments for [Your Stack/Tools], and design a versionable checklist or bootstrap script plan.
In [Tool or Workflow You Use], what manual settings or repetitive clicks can be captured as a reusable config or template instead?

note.zh: 把个人环境配置放进版本控制，让换机与回滚变得可追踪、可复现
note.en: Keeping personal environment configs in version control makes setups reproducible and reversible

title.zh: 让自动化只在“关键决策卡点”停下来等人确认
title.en: Pausing Automation Only at High-Stakes Decision Gates

old_assumption.zh: 自动化要么是“全自动无人值守”，要么是“每一步都弹窗问人”，两者都很别扭。
old_assumption.en: Automation feels like an all-or-nothing choice between blind autonomy and annoying step-by-step prompts.

new_shift.zh: 最顺手的人机协作是：前 90% 的搜集、清洗、草拟全自动跑完，只在涉及对外发送、花钱、删改或高风险判断时留一个清晰确认点。
new_shift.en: The sweet spot is automated research, drafting, and prep—pausing cleanly only before external sends, spend, destructive actions, or high-judgment calls.

zh: 我想把 [某个半自动工作流，如整理信息/起草回复/生成方案] 交给 AI 或脚本跑。请帮我画出“自动执行段”和“必须停下来让我确认的 1～2 个关键卡点”。
针对 [你最担心的自动化翻车场景]，设计一种“低打扰但足够安全”的确认与兜底机制，既不天天弹框烦人又能挡住致命错误。
en: I'm automating [Workflow, e.g., research triage/drafting/planning]. Map what runs automatically vs. the 1–2 decision gates where it should pause for my sign-off.
For [High-Risk Automation Scenario], design a low-noise approval or fallback guard that prevents costly mistakes without constant interruptions.

note.zh: 在关键动作前设置显式确认与护栏，是提升自主工作流可靠性的核心实践
note.en: Explicit human checkpoints before consequential actions keep autonomous workflows trustworthy

title.zh: 给高频 Prompt / 工作流建一份“5 条样例评测集”
title.en: Building a 5-Case Eval Set Before Tweaking Prompts

old_assumption.zh: 改完提示词或工作流，顺手拿手头这一条测一下顺眼就行。
old_assumption.en: After editing a prompt or workflow, testing it on one sample that looks good is enough.

new_shift.zh: 单条样例很容易陷入“修好 A 搞坏 B”；固定 3～5 条典型+刁钻样例做对照，每次改动都能一眼看出是真变强还是只是偏科。
new_shift.en: Testing on one example lets regressions slip through—keeping 3–5 tricky benchmark cases shows whether a tweak actually improves reliability.

zh: 我有一个高频使用的 [Prompt/工作流/自动化规则]：[简述用途]。请帮我设计 4 条覆盖常规、边界与刁钻情况的测试样例，以及一条客观的评分标准。
在 [你的 AI 使用场景] 中，哪些“改了之后偶尔抽风”的提示词最值得先建一套最小评测集再做优化？
en: I have a high-frequency [Prompt, Workflow, or Rule]: [Brief Purpose]. Design 4 test cases (normal, edge, and tricky) plus a clear pass/fail rubric.
In [Your AI Workflow], which prompts or automations drift unexpectedly and would benefit most from a small benchmark set before further tuning?

note.zh: 从真实错误案例中提炼小而精的评测样例，比凭空猜指标更管用
note.en: Small eval sets grounded in real failure cases beat abstract metrics in daily iteration

title.zh: 把核心资产存成“纯文本/JSON”，不被单一工具绑架
title.en: Storing Core Assets in Plain Text & JSON Instead of Walled Gardens

old_assumption.zh: 把笔记、清单和方案全塞进某个热门 App 的私有格式里，方便又省事。
old_assumption.en: Putting notes, trackers, and docs inside a proprietary app's lock-in format is easiest.

new_shift.zh: 工具会涨价、改版、关停或换代，但 Markdown、CSV 和 JSON 跨越几十年依然能被任何编辑器、脚本和 AI 直接读写。
new_shift.en: Tools change pricing, redesign, or shut down—Markdown, CSV, and JSON remain readable by any editor, script, or AI for decades.

zh: 我目前把 [某类重要资料/笔记/清单] 放在 [某个软件或平台] 里。请帮我设计一套导出与落盘为 Markdown / JSON 的结构方案，兼顾可读性与脚本可处理性。
如何让“平时顺手写在某个工具里”和“定期沉淀成跨工具可复用的纯文本/JSON”不变成两张皮？
en: I currently keep [Notes, Trackers, or Docs] inside [App/Platform]. Design a clean Markdown or JSON representation that stays human-readable and script-friendly.
How can I keep quick daily capture effortless while ensuring important records stay portable in plain text or JSON?

note.zh: 文件大于软件：让数据文件成为长期主体，软件只是随时可替换的窗口
note.en: File over app: your files outlive any single app when stored in durable open formats

title.zh: 把大脚本拆成“单一职责的小模块”，靠管道拼装而不是硬写巨石
title.en: Composing Small Single-Purpose Scripts Over Monolithic Automation

old_assumption.zh: 写自动化时习惯把抓取、清洗、判断、输出全塞进一个几百行的庞大脚本里。
old_assumption.en: Automations often bundle fetching, cleaning, filtering, and output into one giant script that's hard to debug or reuse.

new_shift.zh: 每个小模块只干好一件事、输入输出格式清晰，换一个数据源或换一个输出目标时，直接像积木一样重新拼装即可。
new_shift.en: Small tools that each do one job cleanly with clear inputs and outputs snap together like blocks when a source or destination changes.

zh: 我有一个偏臃肿的 [脚本/工作流/自动化任务]：[简述流程]。请帮我拆成 3～4 个职责单一的独立步骤，并定好它们之间传递数据的极简格式。
在 [你的日常自动化场景] 中，哪些“只做一件事的过滤/转换小工具”最值得单独抽出来，方便以后反复复用？
en: I have a sprawling [Script or Workflow]: [Brief Flow]. Break it into 3–4 single-purpose steps with a clean data format passed between them.
In [Your Automation Setup], which small filter or formatter step is worth pulling out as a standalone reusable block?

signals.name: Unix Philosophy — Do One Thing Well

note.zh: 单一职责与标准文本/数据流组合，让小工具拥有极高的复用性与可维护性
note.en: Single-purpose tools linked by clean data streams stay easy to test, swap, and reuse

title.zh: 给 AI 能力配“确定性兜底”，别让偶尔抽风卡死整条流程
title.en: Pairing AI Steps with Deterministic Fallbacks Instead of Brittle Chains

old_assumption.zh: 既然引入了 AI，就让模型从头包揽所有解析、分类和格式化。
old_assumption.en: Once AI is in the loop, let the model handle parsing, routing, and formatting end-to-end every time.

new_shift.zh: 确定性规则能搞定的事别交给概率模型；AI 拿不到预期格式或超时时，自动走规则兜底或跳过留待人工，整条流水线就不会轻易瘫痪。
new_shift.en: Keep deterministic rules where rules suffice, and add clean fallbacks when AI outputs miss format or time out so the whole pipeline keeps moving.

zh: 我有一个依赖 AI 输出的 [工作流/脚本/工具]：[简述用途]，偶尔会出现格式不对或结果偏差。请帮我设计一套“先规则/校验，不行再降级兜底”的安全方案。
审视 [你的某个 AI 应用或工作流]，指出哪两个环节最适合用传统确定性逻辑分担，减少模型的负担与不确定性？
en: My [Workflow or Tool] relies on AI output—[Brief Purpose]—and occasionally slips on format or edge cases. Design a clean validation and fallback path.
Inspect [Your AI Workflow] and point out 2 steps where deterministic rules can share the load and make behavior steadier.

note.zh: 结合校验与优雅降级，能让含 AI 环节的系统在真实使用中更稳健
note.en: Combining schema checks with graceful fallbacks keeps real-world workflows resilient

title.zh: 给脚本和工作流留“结构化痕迹”，出事时 1 分钟定位
title.en: Leaving Structured Traces So Failures Take 1 Minute to Diagnose

old_assumption.zh: 小工具或自动化平时能跑通就行，出错了再临时加打印或靠猜。
old_assumption.en: Small scripts and workflows only need to run when things go right—debug errors by guessing later.

new_shift.zh: 记录关键输入摘要、耗时、跳过原因与最后成功状态，一旦哪天静默失效或结果异常，立刻能顺藤摸瓜找到根因。
new_shift.en: Recording input counts, skip reasons, timings, and last-good state turns mysterious silent failures into a 1-minute root-cause check.

zh: 我有一个日常跑的 [脚本/自动化/工作流]：[简述流程]。帮我设计一套轻量日志与运行摘要格式，既不会把盘塞爆，又能让我在出错时快速定位原因。
在 [你的个人工具或自动化场景] 中，哪些“静默失败（没报错但结果不对）”最隐蔽？如何加一个简单自检提示？
en: I run [Script, Automation, or Workflow]: [Brief Flow]. Design a lightweight run-log format that stays compact while making failures easy to trace.
In [Your Tools or Automations], what kind of 'silent failure' (no crash, wrong result) is hardest to notice, and how can a simple sanity check catch it?

note.zh: 清晰的上下文记录与运行摘要，是降低日常排错成本的高回报习惯
note.en: Clear run summaries and context logs cut debugging time dramatically even in small personal tools

title.zh: 把每天高频切换的 3 个动作绑成顺手快捷键
title.en: Binding Your Top 3 Daily Context Switches to Effortless Hotkeys

old_assumption.zh: 每次打开特定工具、查特定资料或切窗口，多点几下鼠标、多翻几层菜单也差不了几秒。
old_assumption.en: Clicking through menus or hunting windows for frequent tasks only takes a few seconds each time.

new_shift.zh: 每天几十次的微摩擦加起来就是一整块专注力与时间；把最常用的 3 个入口绑成直达快捷键，动作变顺手后使用频率也会自然提高。
new_shift.en: Dozens of tiny micro-frictions add up every day—binding your top 3 recurring actions to instant hotkeys saves time and makes good habits easier to trigger.

zh: 盘点我每天在电脑上最常重复打开或切换的 5 个窗口/工具/动作：[填入你的高频操作]。帮我挑出最值得优先设快捷键的 3 个，并给出无冲突的按键组合建议。
在 [你的常用编辑器/终端/浏览器/启动器] 中，有哪些能把“多步操作”压成“一键触发”的实用小配置？
en: Here are 5 windows, tools, or actions I open or switch to constantly: [List 5 Actions]. Pick the top 3 to bind to shortcuts and suggest conflict-free key combos.
In [Your Editor, Terminal, Browser, or Launcher], what quick config turns a multi-step sequence into a single instant trigger?

note.zh: 减少鼠标往返与菜单寻找，让高频操作接近“想到即触发”
note.en: Cutting menu hunting and mouse detours brings frequent actions close to instant recall

title.zh: 用“显式状态机”约束 Agent 流转，而不是放任自由循环
title.en: Constraining Agent Flows with Explicit State Machines Over Open Loops

old_assumption.zh: 让 Agent 自己决定下一步干什么、循环到满意为止，最接近“真正自主”。
old_assumption.en: Letting an agent freely loop and improvise every next step until it feels done is the most autonomous design.

new_shift.zh: 无界循环容易死循环、烧光预算或偏离轨道；把关键阶段锁进明确状态转移（草稿 → 校验 → 确认 → 执行），自主性更高且可控性呈数量级提升。
new_shift.en: Unbounded loops burn tokens and drift—locking stages into explicit state transitions (draft → verify → approve → act) gives real reliability without losing leverage.

zh: 我有一个多步 [AI 工作流 / Agent 任务]：[简述输入、中间步骤与期望结果]。请帮我画出它的核心状态节点与允许跳转的条件，标出最容易卡死或越界的转移边。
如果把 [你正在搭的某个自动化流程] 改造成带“显式状态与重试上限”的有限状态机，哪些步骤应该允许自动重试，哪些必须直接失败上报？
en: I'm building a multi-step [AI Workflow or Agent Task]: [Describe Inputs, Steps & Target Output]. Map its core states and valid transitions, highlighting where loops or drift can happen.
If I model [My Automation Flow] as an explicit state machine with retry caps, which steps should auto-retry vs. fail fast for human inspection?

note.zh: 强调在自主度与结构化编排之间做务实取舍，比堆砌复杂自由循环更稳健
note.en: Pragmatic workflow structure and clear boundaries outperform uncontrolled loops in production

title.zh: 排查“局部合理却拼出全局僵局”的系统死锁
title.en: Diagnosing System Deadlocks Built Out of Locally Sensible Rules

old_assumption.zh: 只要每个步骤、每个规则单独看都合理安全，拼在一起的系统就不会卡死。
old_assumption.en: If every individual rule or step makes local sense and feels safe, the combined system will work smoothly.

new_shift.zh: 每一步都加缓冲、加审批、加特判，单独看都很聪明，合在一起却可能让整条链路变得迟钝、脆弱甚至无人敢动；要看全局流转而不是单点合理。
new_shift.en: Locally smart buffers, extra checks, and special cases can combine into sluggishness, fragility, or paralysis—inspect end-to-end flow rather than isolated rules.

zh: 梳理我目前常用的 [工作流 / 工具链 / 协作机制]：[简述各环节与规则]。帮我找出哪些“单独看很合理”的规则，合在一起反而制造了等待、绕路或僵局。
如果把 [你觉得有点卡顿或繁琐的流程] 当作一条流转管道来检查，最容易产生“堵车或死锁”的节点在哪里？
en: Map my current [Workflow, Tooling Chain, or Process]: [Describe Steps & Rules]. Find rules that look sensible in isolation but create bottlenecks, detours, or paralysis end-to-end.
Inspect [Slow or Cumbersome Process] as a flow pipeline and spot where congestion or deadlocks actually build up.

note.zh: 系统整体的行为往往由环节间的连接与反馈决定，而非单点局部最优
note.en: Whole-system behavior emerges from connections and delays rather than isolated local optimization

title.zh: “无聊但高客单”的微垂直胶水服务
title.en: Boring, High-Ticket Micro-Glue Services

old_assumption.zh: 赚钱的软件必须做大而全的平台，或者追求海量 C 端流量。
old_assumption.en: Profitable software must be an all-in-one platform or chase massive consumer traffic.

new_shift.zh: 开发成本坍塌后，专门打通两个传统软件数据断层的“小胶水”反而毛利极高、客户留存极稳。
new_shift.en: With near-zero dev costs, tiny glue tools bridging two legacy software silos now offer high margins and sticky retention.

zh: 列出 5 个在 [你的行业/岗位] 中，人们目前必须手动把数据从软件 A 复制粘贴到软件 B 的高频痛点，并评估做成自动化微工具的付费意愿。
针对 [某具体软件生态，如 Shopify/Notion/飞书]，有哪些官方懒得做、但专业用户愿意每月付 20 美元解决的“最后一公里”断层？
en: List 5 high-frequency workflows in [Your Industry] where people manually copy-paste data from App A to App B, and evaluate willingness to pay for an automated glue tool.
Within the [Specific Ecosystem, e.g., Shopify/Notion] ecosystem, what 'last-mile' gaps are too small for the platform to build yet worth $20/mo to power users?

note.zh: 两人自举切入文档分享与追踪痛点，跑出数百万美元 ARR
note.en: 2-person bootstrapped doc-sharing tool reaching multi-million ARR

note.zh: 把传统笨重的表单工具重新做轻，极小团队实现高额盈利
note.en: Lean team reimagining bloated form builders into a beloved indie SaaS

title.zh: 从“按人头卖软件”转向“按结果卖交付”
title.en: Service-as-Software: Pricing by Outcome, Not Seats

old_assumption.zh: B2B 软件的标准商业模式是 SaaS 按席位（per-seat）收费，把工具交给客户自己操作。
old_assumption.en: Standard B2B software charges per-seat subscriptions and leaves the customer to operate the tool.

new_shift.zh: 当 AI 工作流能端到端干完活，客户不再愿意为“多一个登录账号”付钱，而是愿意为“挽回一笔坏账/产出一份合规报告”按结果付费。
new_shift.en: When AI workflows finish the job end-to-end, buyers stop paying for extra logins and happily pay per resolved ticket, recovered invoice, or completed deliverable.

zh: 针对 [某个传统服务行业，如财税/招聘/法务/跨境电商]，拆解一个目前按人工工时收费的环节，设计“AI 自动执行 + 人工兜底 + 按结果计费”的报价结构。
如果我要把 [你的专业技能] 包装成一个“按单交付结果”的产品化服务（Productized Service），最小闭环的定价、交付 SLA 和防扯皮边界该怎么写？
en: Pick a labor-billed task in [Target Industry, e.g., accounting/recruiting/legal] and design an 'AI-executed + human-reviewed + outcome-priced' offer.
If I package [Your Core Skill] into an outcome-based productized service, how should I structure pricing, delivery SLA, and scope boundaries?

note.zh: 率先推行“每成功解决一次客服工单收费 $0.99”的按结果定价
note.en: Pioneered $0.99 per AI-resolved customer support ticket pricing

title.zh: 专拆巨头全家桶里的“10% 核心功能”
title.en: Unbundling the 10% Core Feature from Bloated Giants

old_assumption.zh: 赛道里已经有大厂巨头了，小团队进去就是送人头。
old_assumption.en: If an incumbent giant already owns the category, a solo founder has no chance.

new_shift.zh: 巨头为了服务大企业客户必然越来越臃肿昂贵，精准剥离其中 10% 高频功能并做到极致顺手、价格打三折，反而是最稳的印钞机。
new_shift.en: Giants inevitably bloat to chase enterprise contracts—carving out their top 10% feature with 10x faster UX at a fraction of the price is a proven indie goldmine.

zh: 列出 5 款在 [你熟悉的行业/工作流] 中被用户疯狂吐槽“太重、太贵、功能用不到 10%”的巨头软件，指出每款软件最值得被单独拆出来的核心微功能。
分析 [某款臃肿巨头软件，如 Jira/Salesforce/Photoshop] 在 Reddit 或 G2 上的一星差评，提炼出 3 个独立开发者可以切入的极简替代品切口。
en: List 5 bloated enterprise tools in [Your Industry] where users complain they only use 10% of the features, and identify the sharpest single feature to unbundle.
Analyze the recurring complaints about [Bloated Incumbent, e.g., Jira/Salesforce] and propose 3 focused, fast indie alternatives.

note.zh: 拆解臃肿复杂的 Google Analytics，只做极简隐私友好统计
note.en: Unbundled bloated Google Analytics into a simple, privacy-friendly dashboard

title.zh: 用免费开源/公开工具做“信任漏斗”而非直接卖代码
title.en: Using Free Open Assets as a Trust Funnel Instead of Selling Code

old_assumption.zh: 写了有用的工具或体系就该藏起来收钱，免费公开等于白白送人、没法变现。
old_assumption.en: If you build something useful, keep it proprietary and gated—giving it away for free leaves money on the table.

new_shift.zh: 在软件同质化极高的当下，公开免费工具/知识库是最强的“免许可信任证明”，能把陌生流量自然引向高客单托管、定制服务或进阶工作流。
new_shift.en: When code is abundant, free open tools and libraries act as permissionless proof of competence—converting organic attention into hosted SaaS, services, or pro workflows.

zh: 如果我想在 [你的目标领域] 做一个免费开源的小工具或公开知识库来建立行业信任，设计 3 个“免费层足够好用、付费层省掉麻烦或交付结果”的商业衔接路径。
分析 [某个知名的免费开源/免费工具项目]，拆解它是如何把零散开发者/用户转化为稳定付费客户的，并映射到 [你的场景]。
en: If I launch a free open-source tool or public library in [Target Domain] to build trust, design 3 ways to bridge free users into paid hosted versions, done-for-you workflows, or pro tiers.
Deconstruct how [Notable Free/Open Tool] converts free users into paying customers, and map that funnel onto [Your Domain].

note.zh: 开源日程工具切入市场，通过云托管与企业版实现高增长变现
note.en: Open-source scheduling infrastructure monetized via cloud hosting and team editions

title.zh: 卖“24 小时高密度诊断报告”替代重型咨询
title.en: Selling 24-Hour High-Signal Audits Over Heavy Consulting

old_assumption.zh: 提供专业建议或方案必须拉长战线做几周的大项目、开无数次会，否则显得不够专业。
old_assumption.en: Advisory work requires multi-week engagements and endless discovery calls to feel substantial.

new_shift.zh: AI 把信息收集与初稿梳理压缩到几分钟后，结合个人经验快速指出“哪 3 个卡点正在烧钱/拖慢效率”的固定价格快审，决策门槛极低、利润率极高。
new_shift.en: With AI speeding up research and synthesis, a fixed-price, fast-turnaround audit pinpointing the top 3 leaks or bottlenecks has low buyer friction and high margins.

zh: 结合 [你的专业背景/经验]，设计一款“定价明确、48 小时内交付、聚焦解决 1 个痛点”的微诊断服务（如落地页转化诊断/AI 工作流体检/简历与定位诊断），写出交付物清单。
在 [某垂直人群，如独立开发者/小商家/求职者] 决策花钱前，他们最害怕“花了大钱却没用”；如何用“低价快审 + 抵扣后续合作”降低首单顾虑？
en: Using [Your Expertise], design a fixed-price, 48-hour diagnostic audit targeting one sharp pain point (e.g., funnel teardown, AI workflow audit, positioning review) with concrete deliverables.
How can a fast, low-friction diagnostic audit reduce buyer risk for [Target Audience] and naturally lead to deeper work if they want help executing?

note.zh: 独立创作者高频验证的固定价格产品化审计模式
note.en: Widely validated fixed-scope audit format used by solo founders and specialists

title.zh: 用“单点高频卡点”做楔子切入慢热行业
title.en: Using a Single High-Friction Wedge to Enter Slow Industries

old_assumption.zh: 切入传统行业必须先做一整套全流程系统，否则客户觉得不完整。
old_assumption.en: Entering a traditional industry requires building a full end-to-end suite before customers take you seriously.

new_shift.zh: 传统行业最抗拒推翻整套旧系统，但非常乐意先用一个小工具解决“每天最烦的那一步”；一旦卡住关键数据流，再顺理成章往上下游延伸。
new_shift.en: Slow industries resist ripping out legacy systems, but gladly adopt a sharp wedge that fixes one daily bottleneck—then expand once embedded in the data flow.

zh: 挑选 [某个传统/慢热行业]，找出一个“高频、痛感强、且不涉及核心 ERP 替换”的单点切入楔子，画出“楔子工具 → 沉淀数据 → 扩展工作流”的三步演进路线。
在 [你的目标客户群体] 中，哪些环节一旦自动化就能立刻帮他们省出 3 小时/周或挽回明显损失，最适合作为冷启动的第一个收费切口？
en: Pick [Slow/Traditional Industry] and find a single high-pain wedge that avoids ripping out core systems, then map a 3-step wedge-to-workflow expansion path.
For [Target Buyers], which specific bottleneck saves 3+ hours/week or prevents clear loss immediately, making it the ideal paid wedge?

note.zh: 经典的“楔子切入再扩展”软件增长路径
note.en: Classic wedge-and-expand software go-to-market pattern

title.zh: 先在“极小众垂直圈子”做深价值，而不是一开始买量铺开
title.en: Winning a Tiny Niche Circle Before Chasing Broad Distribution

old_assumption.zh: 新产品或新服务上线就要想办法冲热榜、铺全渠道，用户太少说明没市场。
old_assumption.en: A launch needs broad channels and big reach right away; a tiny audience feels like a non-starter.

new_shift.zh: 在 50～200 个重度痛点用户里成为“真正帮他们省了钱/时间的人”，口碑复利和付费转化率远高于一万个路过围观者。
new_shift.en: Becoming indispensable to 50–200 acute users compounds word-of-mouth and paid conversion far better than 10,000 passive onlookers.

zh: 针对 [你的产品/服务/内容方向]，帮我锁定 3 个“痛点极深、人数不多但能直接触达”的垂直小圈子，并设计第一批 10 个种子用户的真诚触达方式。
如果我只能服务好前 20 个付费用户，我会给他们提供哪些“手动高关怀 + 快速迭代”的专属体验来换取深度反馈和转介绍？
en: For [Your Product/Service/Topic], pinpoint 3 small, reachable communities with acute pain and design an honest outreach plan for your first 10 users.
If you only had to delight your first 20 paying users, what high-touch hands-on help and rapid tweaks would earn referrals and deep insight?

signals.name: Do Things That Don't Scale (Paul Graham)

note.zh: 早期靠高密度一对一服务打磨产品与口碑，是验证真实需求的经典路径
note.en: Early manual, high-touch effort builds real product fit and word-of-mouth before scaling

title.zh: 卖“持续防崩与迭代托管”，而不只是“一锤子交付”
title.en: Selling Ongoing Upkeep & Evolution Instead of One-Off Handoffs

old_assumption.zh: 做外包、定制工具或方案，交付完尾款就结束了，后续维护要么免费扯皮要么没法收钱。
old_assumption.en: Custom builds and advisory end at final handoff—ongoing tweaks turn into unpaid favors or awkward negotiations.

new_shift.zh: 外部接口、平台规则和业务需求都在持续变化，把“每月固定巡检 + 优先微调 + 季度升级”打包成轻量包月，能把波动的接单变成可预测现金流。
new_shift.en: APIs, platforms, and workflows keep shifting—bundling monthly checkups, priority tweaks, and steady iterations turns one-off projects into predictable cashflow.

zh: 结合 [你擅长的技术/设计/运营/自动化能力]，设计一份“低压力、边界清晰”的按月维护与持续优化方案，明确包含什么、不包含什么、多久响应一次。
如何向已经合作过或刚交付完项目的客户，自然提出“后续每月轻量跟进与迭代”的合作选项而不显得推销感太强？
en: Using [Your Skillset], design a low-stress monthly upkeep and iteration retainer with clear boundaries on what's included, excluded, and response cadence.
How can I pitch an optional monthly maintenance and continuous-improvement plan after a project handoff without sounding pushy?

note.zh: 许多独立顾问与开发者靠少量高信任包月客户维持极高自由度与稳定现金流
note.en: Solo operators often sustain high freedom and steady income with a handful of high-trust retainers

title.zh: 用“能算账/能诊断的互动小工具”替代 PDF 白皮书引流
title.en: Interactive Calculators & Diagnostics Over Static Lead Magnets

old_assumption.zh: 做获客或建立专业影响力，要么靠硬广，要么写一份长篇 PDF 资料包让人下载。
old_assumption.en: Attracting interested prospects means ads or gating a generic PDF guide nobody finishes reading.

new_shift.zh: 一个输入几个自家参数就能算出“省多少钱/还差哪一步/存在什么隐患”的极简互动小工具，参与感和转发率远高于静态长文。
new_shift.en: A lightweight interactive calculator or diagnostic where users plug in their own numbers creates immediate personal relevance and natural sharing.

zh: 结合 [你的产品/服务/专业方向]，设计一个“用户只需填 3 个数字或选 4 道题就能拿到定制诊断结果”的极简网页小工具，给出核心公式或打分逻辑。
在 [你的目标客户群体] 中，他们最关心但算不清楚的一笔账或一个风险评估是什么？如何把它做成 1 分钟就能玩出结果的互动页面？
en: For [Your Product, Service, or Expertise], design a tiny interactive calculator or quiz where users enter 3 inputs and get an instant tailored readout.
What cost, savings, or risk is [Target Audience] fuzzy on—and how can I turn it into a 60-second interactive diagnostic?

note.zh: 围绕真实决策算账构建的实用小工具，往往比泛泛的营销文章更有留存与转化力
note.en: Practical calculators tied to real user decisions consistently outperform generic gated content

title.zh: 向愿意为“省时间与确定性”买单的人收溢价
title.en: Monetizing Speed & Certainty When DIY Takes Too Long

old_assumption.zh: 网上很多信息、教程和开源方案都是免费的，所以别人肯定不愿意为同类东西付钱。
old_assumption.en: Since free tutorials and open-source tools exist online, people won't pay for solutions in that space.

new_shift.zh: 免费意味着“自己花时间折腾、自己排错、自己承担试错风险”；对忙碌的个人或小团队来说，花钱买现成省下的时间与确定性本身就是高价值。
new_shift.en: Free usually costs your own hours, debugging, and trial-and-error risk—busy buyers happily pay for speed, polish, and certainty.

zh: 在 [你熟悉的领域] 里，虽然网上有免费教程或开源方案，但新手或忙人自己动手最容易卡在哪 3 步？如何把这 3 步打包成省心的付费方案？
对比“自己从零拼装免费工具”与“直接使用开箱即用的方案”，帮我提炼出对 [某类买家] 最有说服力的 3 个时间/风险价值点。
en: In [Your Domain], free guides exist—where do busy people or newcomers get stuck for hours, and how can a paid offer remove that friction?
Contrast DIY assembling free tools vs. a ready-to-run option, and craft 3 clear time-and-certainty value points for [Target Buyer].

note.zh: 开源或免费方案背后依然存在大量愿意为“省心、免配置、稳定可用”付费的用户
note.en: Even alongside free/open tools, buyers consistently pay for zero-setup convenience and reliability

title.zh: 用一句话说清“帮谁解决什么具体事”，别堆砌形容词
title.en: Stating Who You Help and What Changes in One Plain Sentence

old_assumption.zh: 介绍产品或服务时，词藻越高级、覆盖面越广，听起来就越有分量。
old_assumption.en: Broader claims and lofty buzzwords make a product or service sound more ambitious and credible.

new_shift.zh: 含糊其辞只会让目标用户划走；一句直白写清“目标人群 + 具体痛点/结果 + 为什么现在不同”的话，往往比十句华丽形容词更有成交力。
new_shift.en: Vague buzzwords lose distracted readers—one plain statement of who it's for, what pain or outcome changes, and why now converts far better.

zh: 这是我目前对 [产品/服务/项目] 的介绍：[粘贴你的简介]。请帮我挑出其中的空话和行话，改写成 3 个不同侧重点（省时/省钱/降险）的一句话价值主张。
针对 [你的目标用户]，帮我写出“他们看到第一眼就会觉得‘这说的就是我’”的开场痛点句式。
en: Here is my current pitch for [Product, Service, or Project]: [Paste Pitch]. Strip out buzzwords and write 3 sharp one-sentence value propositions (time, money, or risk).
Draft opening lines for [Target Audience] that immediately signal 'this was built for my exact situation'.

note.zh: 能被普通人 5 秒复述清楚的定位，通常比抽象概念更容易拿到第一批真实反馈
note.en: Positioning someone can repeat accurately in 5 seconds gets cleaner feedback and traction

title.zh: 早期死守“极低固定成本”，别还没验证需求就重装上阵
title.en: Keeping Fixed Costs Near Zero Until Demand Is Proven

old_assumption.zh: 做一件正经事就要先买齐全套高级订阅、折腾复杂架构和精美物料。
old_assumption.en: Starting a serious project means buying pro subscriptions, complex infra, and polished branding upfront.

new_shift.zh: 早期固定成本越低，试错容错率越高、心理压力越小；先用最轻量的方案跑通真实付费或真实使用，有正反馈后再逐步升级。
new_shift.en: Low fixed overhead keeps runway long and pressure low—validate real demand with the leanest stack first, then upgrade once revenue or usage proves it.

zh: 我打算起步做 [你的项目/副业/服务]，目前列出的准备清单是：[列出你打算买的工具或花的时间]。请帮我砍掉非必要项，给出“零/极低固定成本冷启动清单”。
在 [你的启动阶段] 里，哪些钱现在花属于“过早优化/烧钱”，哪些钱花在刀刃上能最快验证真实需求？
en: I'm starting [Project, Side Bet, or Service] and plan to set up: [List Planned Tools/Spend]. Trim non-essentials into a near-zero fixed-cost launch checklist.
At my current stage of [Project], what spending would be premature overhead vs. a high-signal test of real demand?

note.zh: 极简技术栈与低固定成本让单人项目拥有极强的抗风险能力与利润空间
note.en: Lean stacks and low fixed costs give solo builders strong margins and room to experiment

title.zh: 卖“省掉从零搭架子”的起步套件与现成骨架
title.en: Selling Starter Kits That Skip Blank-Page Setup

old_assumption.zh: 大家自己去搜零散教程拼凑也能搭出来，现成的模板或骨架卖不动。
old_assumption.en: People can piece together free guides themselves, so clean starter kits or templates won't sell.

new_shift.zh: 对很多刚起步的人来说，最难的不是写完最后 10%，而是跨过“空白页与环境配置”的冷启动门槛；一套跑得通的骨架能帮他们省掉好几天折腾。
new_shift.en: For many starters, blank-page setup and wiring take days—a working skeleton or starter kit removes early friction and gets them to first results fast.

zh: 结合 [你的技术/设计/运营/写作经验]，找出新手在 [某类项目或任务] 起步时最容易卡住的“空白页/配置环节”，设计一款能让他们 30 分钟跑通第一版的起步套件。
如何让现成模板或起步套件不只是一堆静态文件，而是附带清晰的“10 分钟上手路径与常见坑提示”？
en: Using [Your Experience], spot the blank-page or setup hurdle that slows beginners down in [Domain/Task], and design a starter kit that gets them to a working first run in 30 minutes.
How can a starter kit or template include a crisp 10-minute setup path and pitfall notes so buyers actually get value fast?

note.zh: 把可运行的最小骨架与踩坑经验打包，能显著降低新手的启动成本
note.en: Packaged working skeletons with clear setup notes cut cold-start friction for builders and operators

title.zh: 把价格表砍到“1～2 档明码标价”，别让客户算半天
title.en: Keeping Pricing to 1–2 Clear Tiers Instead of Confusing Matrices

old_assumption.zh: 定价档位分得越细、隐藏条款越多，越显得专业或能把每一分钱榨干。
old_assumption.en: More pricing tiers, complex usage meters, and 'contact us' gates maximize revenue and look enterprise-ready.

new_shift.zh: 复杂的定价表会让犹豫的买家直接关掉页面；一眼看懂“多少钱、包含什么、不适合谁”，反而更容易建立信任并促成下单。
new_shift.en: Convoluted pricing creates decision fatigue and bounce—clear, upfront tiers with plain boundaries build trust and speed up buying.

zh: 这是我目前对 [产品/服务/合作方案] 的定价或收费想法：[简述方案]。请帮我把它简化成 1～2 档一眼看懂的方案，并写清“适合谁 / 暂不适合谁”。
在 [你的目标客户决策场景] 中，哪些定价细节最容易让人产生“是不是还有隐形收费”的顾虑？如何用直白的话提前说清？
en: Here is how I'm thinking about pricing [Product, Service, or Offer]: [Brief Details]. Simplify it into 1–2 crystal-clear options with who each fits best.
What pricing ambiguities make [Target Buyers] hesitate or worry about hidden extras, and how can I state terms plainly upfront?

note.zh: 清晰、可预测、无套路的定价结构，往往能降低独立产品与服务的成交阻力
note.en: Straightforward, predictable pricing lowers buyer hesitation for lean products and services

title.zh: 把“给所有人用”收窄成“专为某类具体人解决某件事”
title.en: Narrowing 'For Everyone' to One Specific Person and Job

old_assumption.zh: 受众写得越宽，潜在客户就越多，缩窄人群等于主动放弃市场。
old_assumption.en: Targeting a broad audience maximizes potential buyers; narrowing down feels like shrinking your market.

new_shift.zh: 泛泛而谈很难让人觉得“这东西是给我做的”；一旦切准某一类具体人群的特定场景，文案、功能和获客渠道都会变得异常清晰。
new_shift.en: Generic pitches get scrolled past—naming one specific buyer and situation makes messaging, features, and outreach dramatically sharper.

zh: 我目前面向的受众/客户群有点宽：[简述你的产品、服务或内容方向]。请帮我拆出 3 个更具体的细分人群切口，并说明每个切口最突出的痛点。
针对 [你选定的一个细分人群]，帮我写出他们日常最常抱怨的一句话，以及能直接回应这句话的产品/服务切入点。
en: My current audience feels a bit broad: [Describe Product, Service, or Topic]. Carve out 3 sharper sub-niches and highlight the clearest pain point in each.
For [Chosen Sub-Niche], write a complaint they actually voice day to day and a focused angle that solves it directly.

note.zh: 早期聚焦具体人群与具体痛点，往往比一上来做大而全更容易赢得第一批铁粉
note.en: Focusing early on a concrete user and workflow beats broad generality when finding traction

title.zh: 把“每次帮客户/自己重复做”的方案，抽成可复用的标准化产品
title.en: Productizing Repeated Custom Work Into a Repeatable Offer

old_assumption.zh: 每次合作或每个需求情况都不一样，只能从头定制、一事一议。
old_assumption.en: Every client or task has unique quirks, so everything must be scoped and built custom from scratch.

new_shift.zh: 做过 5 次以上的同类定制里，往往 70% 的步骤和骨架都是重复的；把这 70% 固化成标准流程与模板，交付更快、毛利更高。
new_shift.en: After doing similar custom work 5+ times, ~70% of the steps and structure repeat—standardizing that core speeds delivery and lifts margins.

zh: 盘点我过去做过的 [咨询/开发/设计/分析/整理] 工作中，哪些类型出现了至少 3 次以上？帮我找出其中可标准化的 70% 骨架与 30% 可定制项。
如何把一份原本靠“一对一沟通定制”的方案，改造成有清晰步骤、交付清单和固定周期的产品化服务？
en: Look across [Consulting, Dev, Design, Analysis, or Ops] tasks I've done 3+ times—separate the repeatable 70% core from the custom 30%.
How can I package a bespoke, one-off service into a repeatable offer with clear steps, deliverables, and turnaround time?

note.zh: 用标准化流程与清晰边界替代纯定制，是个人把经验变成可复制收入的经典路径
note.en: Replacing custom-from-scratch work with clear steps and deliverables creates healthier leverage

title.zh: 把产品/服务“嵌进别人每天必看的结果页”里自带分发
title.en: Embedding Distribution Inside Outputs People Already Share or Inspect

old_assumption.zh: 获客是产品做完之后的独立营销动作，靠发帖、投流或到处求人转发。
old_assumption.en: Growth happens after building by posting updates, buying ads, or asking people to share.

new_shift.zh: 当用户每次导出报告、生成分享链接、跑完检查或展示结果时，页面自带极克制的来源标识或可复现入口，每次使用都在替你做自然触达。
new_shift.en: When a tool's output, shared link, or check report carries a clean source badge or 'run this on yours' link, every use quietly creates distribution.

zh: 针对 [你的工具/模板/分析服务/内容形式]，设计 2 个“用户正常使用时顺便把价值带给下一个潜在用户”的自然嵌入机制，要求不恶心、不破坏体验。
盘点 [你熟悉的几款高增长独立工具]，它们在“分享链接 / 导出结果 / 报错或完成页”上藏了哪些聪明的分发细节？
en: For [Your Tool, Template, Service, or Format], design 2 non-intrusive ways normal usage exposes the value to the next potential user or collaborator.
Look at [Indie Tools You Admire]—what subtle distribution hooks live on their shared links, exports, or completion states?

note.zh: 高频交付物自带轻量来源链接，让每一次真实使用都成为可信的口碑曝光
note.en: Clean attribution on shared artifacts turns everyday user activity into organic discovery

title.zh: 先验证“买家默认不愿意改变的习惯”，再打磨功能
title.en: Testing Habits Buyers Refuse to Change Before Polishing Features

old_assumption.zh: 只要产品功能够全、界面够好，解决痛点后用户自然会切换过来。
old_assumption.en: Once features are solid and UI is clean, users will naturally switch when the pain is real.

new_shift.zh: 人们最抗拒的往往不是“没好工具”，而是“改变现有习惯、迁移历史数据或承担切换风险”；先测清他们宁愿忍受什么也不改，才能找准真正能落地的切口。
new_shift.en: Switching costs, habit inertia, and migration fear often block adoption even when a tool is better—test what buyers refuse to change before building deep features.

zh: 针对 [你的目标用户/客户群体] 在 [某场景] 下的现状：[简述他们现在怎么凑合做]。帮我列出 4 个可能导致他们“懒得切换”的习惯阻力或迁移顾虑，以及低成本验证方法。
在 [你的产品或服务设想] 中，哪一个“需要用户改变原有习惯”的动作最容易卡住转化？
en: For [Target Buyers] handling [Workflow] today—[Describe Current Workaround]—list 4 habit or switching frictions that could keep them put, plus cheap ways to test them.
In [Product or Service Idea], which required habit shift is most likely to stall early adoption?

note.zh: 及早看清用户既有习惯与迁移阻力，能避免把精力花在“叫不醒装睡的习惯”上
note.en: Spotting habit inertia and switching friction early saves building features users won't adopt

title.zh: 把私有工作流直接转化为公开内容资产
title.en: Turning Private Workflows into Public Content Assets

old_assumption.zh: 做内容必须专门抽出额外时间“憋选题、写长文、剪视频”。
old_assumption.en: Creating content requires carving out separate time to brainstorm topics, write essays, or film videos.

new_shift.zh: 在 AI 垃圾文章泛滥的时代，把你日常解决问题沉淀下来的结构化清单、分类库、Prompt 和工具直接开源展示，才是最具传播力的硬通货。
new_shift.en: In a sea of AI slop, publishing the real checklists, taxonomies, prompts, and mini-tools you already built for yourself earns far higher trust and shares.

zh: 我平时在工作/生活中反复做的一件事是：[描述你的具体事情]。请帮我把它拆解成一个可复用的公开资产（模板/静态卡片库/清单），并设计 3 个能让同行主动转发的切入点。
如何把 [你的某个日常研究/踩坑记录] 改造成一个可交互、可搜索的极简网页合集，让它从一次性文章变成长期带来自然流量的资产？
en: I repeatedly do [Specific Task] in my work/life. Help me package this process into a reusable public asset (template, checklist, or static library) with 3 angles peers will actually share.
How can I turn my raw notes on [Your Topic] into a searchable, interactive mini-site that compounds organic traffic instead of dying in a social feed?

note.zh: 将个人高频 AI 工作流与提示词沉淀为可检索的公开卡片库
note.en: Personal AI workflows packaged as a searchable public card library

title.zh: 反算法推荐的“交互式网页玩具”内容
title.en: Interactive Web Toys & Explorable Explanations

old_assumption.zh: 传播观点和获取流量只能靠图文、短视频和播客去卷平台算法。
old_assumption.en: Spreading ideas and earning attention means fighting social algorithms with text threads or short videos.

new_shift.zh: AI 让单人做出精巧的交互式小网页门槛骤降，一个能让用户亲手点 3 分钟的“可玩概念”，传播穿透力远超一万字长文。
new_shift.en: AI collapsed the cost of interactive frontends—a 3-minute playable web toy or simulator spreads organically far better than a 3,000-word essay.

zh: 我想向大众解释一个复杂概念：[填入你想讲的概念]。请帮我设计 3 个“可交互网页玩具/小游戏”的玩法原型，让用户玩 2 分钟就能彻底悟懂。
针对 [你的目标受众，如程序员/理财新手/英语学习者]，设计一个带有反差幽默感、用户玩完会忍不住截图发朋友圈的极简网页小测试。
en: I want to explain [Complex Concept] intuitively. Propose 3 interactive web-toy or mini-simulator mechanics that let users grasp it by playing for 2 minutes.
For [Target Audience], design a playful, slightly absurd single-page web interactive whose result screen naturally makes people share screenshots.

note.zh: 独立开发者靠一系列脑洞网页小玩具持续获得亿级自然传播
note.en: Indie creator driving hundreds of millions of organic visits through pure web toys

note.zh: 用交互式模拟取代静态文章的“可探索式解释”合集
note.en: Curated hub of interactive essays and playable simulations

title.zh: 极高密度的“反过载策展”替代泛资讯搬运
title.en: High-Density Anti-Slop Curation Over Volume Publishing

old_assumption.zh: 做自媒体必须保持日更、追热点，靠更新频率维持存在感。
old_assumption.en: Creators must post daily and chase trending news to stay relevant.

new_shift.zh: 内容供给无限趋近于免费后，受众最稀缺的不是“多看一篇”，而是有人替他们狠心删掉 99% 噪音、只留 1% 经过实测验证的精选。
new_shift.en: When content volume is infinite and free, audiences don't want more posts—they pay attention to curators who ruthlessly delete 99% of the noise.

zh: 在 [你关注的垂直领域] 里，大家每天都被哪些低质重复信息轰炸？帮我设计一份“每月只发一次、但每条都经过实测验证”的高密度策展专栏结构。
如何为 [某垂直主题] 设计一套透明的“入选红线与淘汰标准”，让读者一眼看出我的推荐库和普通搬运号有本质区别？
en: What repetitive noise floods [Your Niche] every week? Design a low-frequency, ultra-high-density curation format where every item is hands-on verified.
Draft a transparent 'inclusion & rejection rubric' for a curated library on [Your Topic] so readers immediately trust its signal-to-noise ratio.

note.zh: 独立策展周刊，靠极高的审美与信息密度积累了忠实全球读者
note.en: Independent curated newsletter thriving on taste and signal density

title.zh: 借多模态降本创造“图文+声音+交互”新体裁
title.en: Inventing Hybrid Formats as Multimodal Creation Collapses

old_assumption.zh: 做音视频、配乐或动态演示需要专业设备和剪辑团队，个人创作者只能死磕纯文字。
old_assumption.en: Producing audio, video, music, or motion requires gear and editing skills—solo creators should stick to plain text.

new_shift.zh: 文本、语音、音乐与可视化生成成本大幅下降后，把“短洞察 + 氛围音频/微型演示”组合在一起的混合体裁，更容易在信息流里形成独特记忆点。
new_shift.en: As audio, music, and visual generation get cheaper, pairing sharp ideas with ambient sound, voice, or lightweight motion creates distinct sensory hooks in crowded feeds.

zh: 我想为 [某个主题/情绪，如深夜复盘/极客科普/放松解压] 创作内容。设计一种结合“文字 + 声音/音乐/视觉动效”的轻量混合体裁，给出单人 30 分钟内可复制的生产流程。
分析目前 [你常刷的内容平台] 上同质化最严重的表达方式，设计 2 个反常规但能保留高信息密度的混合表达形式。
en: I want to create content around [Topic/Mood, e.g., late-night reflection/tech explainers/calm focus]. Design a lightweight text + audio/music/visual format I can produce solo in 30 minutes.
Spot the most repetitive content cliché on [Platform You Use], and invent 2 distinct hybrid formats that keep high information density.

note.zh: 用数据可视化与交互叙事讲故事，让复杂议题变得极易沉浸阅读
note.en: Visual and interactive journalism turning dense topics into memorable stories

title.zh: 做“随手可查的常青手册”而非“保质期 48 小时的热点”
title.en: Building Evergreen Reference Hubs Instead of 48-Hour News

old_assumption.zh: 内容要靠追当天热点和情绪共鸣才能拿到点击和关注。
old_assumption.en: Content needs breaking news hooks and emotional spikes to get traction.

new_shift.zh: 热点 48 小时就凉，但一份结构清晰、边界明确的“避坑对照表 / 决策清单 / 术语词典”会在未来几年被反复收藏、搜索和引用。
new_shift.en: Breaking news dies in 48 hours, while a crisp comparison table, decision checklist, or field glossary gets bookmarked, searched, and cited for years.

zh: 在 [你的专业或兴趣领域] 中，新手或从业者最容易反复查错、踩坑的 10 个概念或决策点是什么？帮我搭一份“常青速查手册”的目录大纲。
把一篇我以前写过、但很快沉底的观点文章：[简述文章核心]，改写成一张“结构化决策矩阵/避坑清单”，提升它的长期复用价值。
en: In [Your Domain], what are the 10 concepts, traps, or decisions people repeatedly look up or get wrong? Outline an evergreen quick-reference guide.
Transform a past post of mine on [Topic] into a reusable decision matrix or checklist that stays useful months and years later.

note.zh: 高结构化参考文档之所以拥有极长生命周期，在于它直接服务“正在解决问题的瞬间”
note.en: Reference guides endure because they serve people right at the moment of solving a problem

title.zh: 写“带明确取舍立场”的对比测评，而不是骑墙水文
title.en: Writing Opinionated Trade-Off Comparisons Over Fence-Sitting Reviews

old_assumption.zh: 做评测或对比要面面俱到、各方都不得罪，列出“各有优缺点”就算客观。
old_assumption.en: Comparisons should stay neutral and list pros and cons for every option so nobody disagrees.

new_shift.zh: AI 能瞬间生成“各方面都差不多”的骑墙总结，读者真正需要的是：在明确场景下，“我选 A 放弃 B 的真实理由和踩坑边界”。
new_shift.en: AI easily writes neutral 'both have pros and cons' summaries—readers value a clear stance on why you pick A over B for specific scenarios and where that choice hurts.

zh: 针对 [两个你熟悉的工具/方案/方法，如 A vs B]，不要写水端平的优缺点列表。请按“什么人选 A、什么人选 B、各自最隐蔽的坑”帮我梳理一份立场鲜明的对比框架。
针对 [某个热门工具或流行做法]，帮我列出 3 个“主流吹捧但实际有明显代价”的细节，写出诚实且有洞察的边界说明。
en: For [Option A vs. Option B], skip balanced fluff. Structure a sharp trade-off guide covering who should pick A, who should pick B, and the hidden catch in each.
For [Popular Tool or Practice], identify 3 overhyped claims and the real trade-offs or edge cases people only discover after adopting it.

note.zh: 讲清楚“为什么选它、什么时候别选它”的技术与产品对比最容易引发深度讨论
note.en: Trade-off breakdowns explaining both fit and failure modes consistently earn high-signal discussion

title.zh: 写“亲手踩坑与真实实验日志”，而不是空洞方法论
title.en: Publishing Real Experiment Logs Over Abstract Frameworks

old_assumption.zh: 要把一个道理讲透，得先搭一套高大上的“三层模型/五步法则”再包装成金句。
old_assumption.en: Authoritative content requires wrapping ideas in a catchy 5-step framework and bold takeaways.

new_shift.zh: AI 最擅长拼凑“看起来很对的五步法则”，却无法替代你亲手试错后的真实数据、失败截图和意外转折——真实实验日志自带稀缺感。
new_shift.en: AI excels at generic 5-step frameworks; firsthand logs with real numbers, failed attempts, and unexpected turns carry genuine scarcity.

zh: 我最近做了一次真实尝试或踩坑：[简述你试了什么、发生了什么意外]。帮我把它整理成一篇诚实、克制、有细节的“实验记录”，去掉空洞鸡汤。
在 [你的领域] 里，有哪些“书本和教程里很少写、但实战中经常遇到”的真实细节，适合写成短小精悍的实战笔记？
en: I recently ran a real experiment or hit a snag: [Describe What Happened & Any Surprises]. Shape it into a candid, detail-rich field log without generic fluff.
In [Your Domain], what messy real-world details rarely make it into tutorials would make sharp, credible field notes?

note.zh: 坦诚复盘“哪里没想全、怎么修好的”的技术与产品日志往往最具借鉴价值
note.en: Candid postmortems detailing what broke and how it was fixed teach far more than polished hype

title.zh: 先沉淀“原子知识块”，再按需组装成不同形态输出
title.en: Authoring Atomic Building Blocks Before Assembling Formats

old_assumption.zh: 每次输出都要从空白文档开始写起，写完这篇再想下一篇写什么。
old_assumption.en: Every piece of content starts from a blank page, then you start from scratch for the next one.

new_shift.zh: 把洞察、案例、对比和 Prompt 拆成独立的“原子块”存好，需要发短动态、做卡片库或写深度指南时直接拼装，边际创作成本大幅下降。
new_shift.en: Storing insights, examples, trade-offs, and prompts as modular atomic blocks lets you assemble cards, threads, or guides with far less friction.

zh: 帮我设计一套极简的“个人内容原子块”分类方式（如：反常识对比 / 真实案例 / 实用清单 / 提问模板），让我平时随手记一条，以后能快速拼装成多种内容。
把这段我已经写好的零散内容：[粘贴内容]，拆解成 3～4 个可独立复用的“原子知识块”。
en: Design a simple schema of 'atomic content blocks' (e.g., contrast, case study, checklist, prompt) so quick jottings can be recombined into cards or essays later.
Break this rough draft—[Paste Draft]—into 3–4 standalone atomic blocks I can reuse across different formats.

note.zh: 把大块写作拆成可独立成立的最小单元，降低启动阻力并提高复用率
note.en: Breaking writing into self-contained units lowers friction and boosts long-term reuse

title.zh: 用一张“结构图/流程图”讲清复杂关系，少写 800 字解释
title.en: Explaining Complex Systems with One Diagram Instead of 800 Words

old_assumption.zh: 把一件复杂的事讲清楚，需要靠层层递进的长段落和严密的文字修辞。
old_assumption.en: Explaining intricate mechanics requires long paragraphs and careful prose transitions.

new_shift.zh: 因果回路、状态流转和层级关系用一张干净的示意图或对比图表达，往往 5 秒就能看懂全貌，转发率和收藏率也更高。
new_shift.en: Flows, feedback loops, and architectures click in seconds via a clean diagram—often outperforming walls of text in clarity and saves.

zh: 我想把 [某个复杂机制/工作流/概念关系] 讲清楚。请帮我设计一张“信息图/流程图/象限图”的版面结构，标出核心节点、连线关系和一句点睛标题。
把下面这段偏抽象的文字说明：[粘贴文字]，改写成适合画成示意图的“节点 + 关系 + 关键结论”结构。
en: I want to explain [Complex Mechanism, Workflow, or Relationship]. Design a clean diagram layout (flow, loop, or matrix) with nodes, arrows, and a punchy title.
Convert this text explanation—[Paste Text]—into a diagram-ready outline of nodes, relationships, and the core takeaway.

note.zh: 把抽象观念压缩成视觉符号与结构图，能显著降低跨背景理解成本
note.en: Compressing abstract ideas into visual diagrams lowers comprehension friction across audiences

title.zh: 做“有清晰演进弧线的系列”，而不是互不相关的单篇拼盘
title.en: Building Connected Series with an Arc Instead of Disjointed One-Offs

old_assumption.zh: 每篇内容都当成独立单篇来发，只要单篇爆了就行，前后有没有关联无所谓。
old_assumption.en: Treat every post as a standalone lottery ticket—how it connects to previous or next posts doesn't matter.

new_shift.zh: 前后呼应、层层递进的系列（比如从“认知破盲 → 方案设计 → 实战踩坑 → 复盘迭代”）更容易让读者产生“追更”习惯并沉淀成合集资产。
new_shift.en: A connected series—moving from blindspot to design, real execution, and lessons learned—builds reader habit and compounds into a cohesive guide.

zh: 围绕 [你想深挖的一个核心主题]，帮我规划一个 5 篇左右的“递进式系列大纲”，每篇承担不同的推进作用（破盲/拆解/动手/避坑/总结）。
如何把我已经写过的几篇零散内容：[列出主题或链接]，重新串联成一份带导读和学习路径的“主题合集”？
en: Outline a 5-part progressive series around [Core Theme] where each installment advances the reader (blindspot, breakdown, hands-on, pitfalls, synthesis).
How can I weave several standalone posts on [Topic] into a structured series with a clear reading path?

note.zh: 有节奏感的系列连载能把单次点击转化为持续关注与完整阅读
note.en: A structured series turns occasional readers into returning followers completing a journey

title.zh: 每讲一个抽象道理，立刻配一个“具体前后对比例子”
title.en: Pairing Every Abstract Claim with a Concrete Before/After Example

old_assumption.zh: 道理讲得够深刻、够道理，读者自然会自己脑补怎么用。
old_assumption.en: If the principle is smart enough, readers will figure out how to apply it on their own.

new_shift.zh: 抽象道理看完容易忘，但一个“改前 vs 改后”的真实例子（一段前后对比的文字、一个截图、一条具体 Prompt）能让读者立刻看懂并照着做。
new_shift.en: Abstract principles fade fast; a concrete before/after example—a rewritten snippet, workflow diff, or real prompt—makes the idea immediately usable.

zh: 我打算写一篇围绕 [你的核心观点] 的内容，但目前有点偏空泛。请帮我为这个观点设计 2 个贴近 [目标读者] 日常场景的“前后对比案例”。
检查下面这段草稿：[粘贴草稿]，指出哪几句最抽象、最像空话，并帮我改写成带具体动作或样例的表达。
en: I'm writing about [Core Idea], and it feels a bit abstract. Create 2 concrete before/after examples tailored to [Target Reader].
Spot the most abstract or hand-wavy sentences in [Paste Draft] and rewrite them with specific, grounded examples.

signals.name: Show, Don't Tell in Technical & Indie Writing

note.zh: 用具体示例、对比与步骤拆解抽象概念，是降低阅读门槛最直接的方式
note.en: Concrete examples and side-by-side diffs make complex ideas graspable right away

title.zh: 开头前三句直击“读者关心的切口”，而不是先交代背景流水账
title.en: Opening With the Reader's Stake Instead of Backstory Warm-Ups

old_assumption.zh: 文章或分享开头应该先铺垫历史背景、个人心路或“最近我一直在想……”。
old_assumption.en: Good intros start with background context, personal backstory, or 'Lately I've been thinking about...'

new_shift.zh: 读者在信息流里只有几秒决定留不留；前三句就点出“什么反常识现象 / 什么痛点 / 能帮他们解决什么”，留存率会高出很多。
new_shift.en: Readers decide in seconds whether to stay—leading with the core tension, surprise, or payoff earns attention far faster than a slow warm-up.

zh: 这是我准备发的一篇内容/分享的开头：[粘贴开头]。请帮我砍掉慢热的背景铺垫，改写出 3 个直接切中要害、克制不浮夸的开头版本。
围绕 [你想分享的主题]，帮我写出 3 个“直击痛点或反常识反差”的第一句话。
en: Here is my draft opening for [Topic]: [Paste Opening]. Cut slow warm-ups and write 3 sharp, grounded openings that hook the reader immediately.
Give me 3 crisp opening lines for [Topic] that highlight a real tension or counter-intuitive shift without clickbait.

note.zh: 开篇即给出清晰张力或独特切角，能显著提升完整读完率
note.en: Leading with clear tension or a sharp angle improves completion rates over throat-clearing intros

title.zh: 提炼“最颠覆你认知的 2～3 点”，而不是逐章流水账摘要
title.en: Distilling 2–3 Core Shifts Instead of Chapter-by-Chapter Summaries

old_assumption.zh: 写书评、读后感或长文拆解，要把每一章、每一段的核心要点都列全才算完整。
old_assumption.en: Good book or essay notes summarize every chapter and bullet point so nothing is missed.

new_shift.zh: 面面俱到的摘要既枯燥又容易变成 AI 就能生成的复述；挑出真正改变你视角或做法的 2～3 个点展开深聊，反而更有灵魂和辨识度。
new_shift.en: Exhaustive summaries read like AI recaps—focusing deeply on the 2–3 ideas that actually shifted your thinking or habits creates sharper, more original notes.

zh: 我刚看完 [一本书/一篇长文/一场分享]：[简述核心内容与你印象最深的点]。请帮我挑出最值得聊的 2 个切角，写成一篇克制、有个人视角的心得大纲。
把下面这段偏流水账的阅读笔记：[粘贴笔记]，删掉重复概括，保留最反常识或最能指导行动的洞察。
en: I just finished [Book, Essay, or Talk]: [Brief Summary & Standout Points]. Pick the 2 sharpest angles and outline a thoughtful, personal note.
Trim this chapter-by-chapter summary—[Paste Notes]—cutting repetitive recap and highlighting the 2–3 insights with real leverage.

note.zh: 少即是多：围绕少数真正触动自己的洞见做连接，比全量摘录更容易沉淀真知
note.en: Focusing on a few resonant ideas and connecting them to practice beats exhaustive copying

title.zh: 结尾给一个“5 分钟就能试的小动作”，别只留一句空泛升华
title.en: Ending with a 5-Minute Tryable Step Instead of Vague Grandstanding

old_assumption.zh: 文章或分享结尾应该拔高立意、抒情总结或喊一句口号才算收尾。
old_assumption.en: Posts should wrap up with a sweeping philosophical climax or inspiring slogan.

new_shift.zh: 赞同感几分钟就会淡去；结尾给一个 5 分钟就能试的小动作或自检问题，读者更容易真正带走改变。
new_shift.en: Agreement fades in minutes; ending with one 5-minute action or self-check helps readers actually apply what they read.

zh: 这是我准备发布的一篇内容/分享正文：[粘贴正文或核心要点]。请帮我写一个不矫情、不拔高的结尾，附带 1 个读者 5 分钟内就能动手试的小动作。
针对 [你常写的某类主题内容]，帮我设计 3 种不同风格的“结尾行动钩子”（如自测题/小实验/反向思考）。
en: Here is my draft post on [Topic]: [Paste Draft or Key Points]. Write a grounded ending with one concrete 5-minute step the reader can try right away.
Give me 3 natural ending prompts (a quick self-check, tiny experiment, or contrast question) for readers of [Your Topic].

note.zh: 把抽象建议落到具体、微小的下一步动作上，能显著提升内容的实用留存
note.en: Translating insights into a small, concrete next step makes ideas stick in daily life

title.zh: 从“别人真正在问的问题”里找选题，而不是闭门造车猜热门
title.en: Sourcing Topics from Real Questions People Actually Ask

old_assumption.zh: 想写内容时坐在电脑前硬想选题，或者去翻别人爆了什么标题跟着写。
old_assumption.en: Brainstorming topics in a vacuum or copying viral headlines without knowing what people actually struggle with.

new_shift.zh: 评论区、私信、群聊里的真实困惑和卡点，往往藏着最贴近现实的需求；把高频真问题整理成解答或指南，天然就有共鸣和实用价值。
new_shift.en: Real questions in comments, DMs, and threads point straight to genuine confusion and friction—answering them directly creates high-relevance content.

zh: 这是我最近在 [评论区/群聊/私信/日常交流] 听到的几个真实问题或困惑：[粘贴 3-5 条真实提问]。请帮我归类并提炼出 2～3 个值得写透的内容切口。
针对 [你的专业或兴趣方向]，新手和进阶者最常卡住但不好意思开口问的 5 个问题是什么？
en: Here are 3–5 real questions or confusions I recently encountered around [Topic]: [Paste Questions]. Group them and propose 2–3 high-value content angles.
In [Your Domain], what are 5 common stumbling blocks beginners or peers struggle with quietly that deserve a clear, practical breakdown?

note.zh: 围绕真实困惑展开解答，能让内容直接对准读者当下的卡点
note.en: Anchor topics around real questions so content meets readers right where they are stuck

title.zh: 写完初稿后狠心删掉 30% 废话，留下的往往更有力量
title.en: Cutting 30% of the Fluff After a First Draft Makes Ideas Hit Harder

old_assumption.zh: 内容越长、铺垫越多、解释越细，才越显得充实和认真。
old_assumption.en: Longer drafts with extra qualifiers and throat-clearing feel more thorough and complete.

new_shift.zh: 把重复的过渡句、空洞修饰词和绕弯子的铺垫删掉之后，核心观点会更锋利，读者的阅读负担也轻了一大截。
new_shift.en: Trimming redundant transitions, filler qualifiers, and wind-ups sharpens the core point and respects the reader's time.

zh: 这是我刚写完的一段草稿：[粘贴草稿]。请帮我删掉重复和水分，保留原意与个人语气，给出一个更精炼、更有节奏感的版本。
帮我检查这段文字：[粘贴文字]，标出哪些句子属于“可有可无的铺垫或重复”，并说明为什么可以删掉。
en: Here is a rough draft: [Paste Draft]. Cut filler and repetition while keeping the core meaning and voice, returning a tighter, cleaner version.
Review [Paste Text], highlight sentences that add fluff or repeat earlier points, and explain how trimming them sharpens the piece.

note.zh: 先放开写初稿、再克制删减修饰语，是提升表达清晰度最稳妥的节奏
note.en: Drafting freely first and trimming excess later keeps writing both natural and crisp

title.zh: 用“弱信号源”替代“算法新闻源”
title.en: Replacing News Feeds with a Weak-Signal Radar

old_assumption.zh: 保持敏锐的方式是每天刷热搜、科技媒体和公众号推送。
old_assumption.en: Staying sharp means checking tech news, social feeds, and trending topics daily.

new_shift.zh: 媒体报道的永远是已经卷成红海的“滞后共识”；真正的早期变化藏在 GitHub 提交记录、小众论坛吐槽、产品更新日志和论文附录里。
new_shift.en: Media reports lagging consensus; real early shifts hide in GitHub commits, niche forum complaints, changelogs, and paper appendices.

zh: 我想持续追踪 [某个具体领域] 最早期的真实变化，但不想看二手媒体通稿。请帮我列出 5 个高信噪比的一手弱信号来源，以及每周 15 分钟的扫描方法。
把下面这段我刷到的零散观察：[粘贴你的观察或链接]，往上抽象一层：它背后反映的底层结构变化是什么？在哪些相邻领域可能出现类似机会？
en: I want to track early shifts in [Specific Field] without reading secondhand media hype. Give me 5 high-signal primary sources and a 15-minute weekly scanning routine.
Abstract this raw observation up one level: [Paste Observation]. What structural shift does it signal, and what adjacent domains might be affected next?

note.zh: 大量独立开发者与前沿实验项目的最早一手发布阵地
note.en: Primary early-stage launchpad for indie tools and frontier experiments

title.zh: 把 AI 当“红队死对头”而不是“顺从助手”
title.en: Using AI as an Adversarial Red-Teamer, Not a Yes-Man

old_assumption.zh: 遇到决策纠结时，让 AI 帮自己补充论据、优化方案、给点鼓励。
old_assumption.en: When making decisions, people ask AI to polish their plan and validate their reasoning.

new_shift.zh: 大模型默认讨好用户（Sycophancy），它最被低估的用法其实是强制它扮演冷酷的反对派，在投入时间前先做“事前验尸（Pre-mortem）”。
new_shift.en: LLMs default to sycophancy—their most underused superpower is role-playing a ruthless skeptic to run a pre-mortem before you commit months of effort.

zh: 我正打算做这个决定/项目：[描述你的想法]。请收起礼貌和鼓励，扮演最挑剔的行业老兵，给出 5 个最可能导致这件事在 3 个月内彻底失败的致命盲区。
针对我的判断：[填入你的核心观点]，帮我构建一个最强版本的反方论证（Steelman），并指出只需要验证哪 1 个事实就能推翻我现在的假设。
en: I am about to commit to [Your Decision/Project]. Drop all politeness and act as a ruthless domain veteran: give me the 5 sharpest reasons this fails within 3 months.
Build the strongest possible counter-argument (Steelman) against my belief that [Your Belief], and identify the single falsifiable test that would prove me wrong.

signals.name: Gary Klein — Performing a Project Premortem (HBR)

note.zh: 经典决策方法“事前验尸”：假设项目已经失败，倒推最可能的死因
note.en: Classic decision method: assume the project failed and work backward to find hidden flaws

title.zh: 用“结构同构”做跨学科解法移植
title.en: Cross-Domain Solution Transfer via Structural Analogy

old_assumption.zh: 遇到难题时，只在自己所在行业的最佳实践里找答案。
old_assumption.en: When stuck on a hard problem, look only at best practices inside your own industry.

new_shift.zh: 你所在领域卡了十年的难题，往往在另一个毫不相干的学科（如航空、生态学、游戏设计、精益制造）里早就有成熟到烂大街的标准解法。
new_shift.en: A problem your industry has struggled with for a decade is often already a solved textbook pattern in aviation, ecology, game design, or manufacturing.

zh: 我目前卡在一个难题上：[描述你的问题，去掉行业黑话]。请先把这个问题抽象成底层结构，再从 3 个完全不相关的领域（如游戏设计、急诊医学、航空管制、生态学）找出成熟解法并翻译回来。
如果把 [你正在做的项目/习惯] 当作一款电子游戏的机制来重新设计，有哪些“即时反馈、难度曲线、防挫败”的设计可以直接照搬过来？
en: I am stuck on [Describe Problem Without Jargon]. Abstract it to its core mechanics, then transplant proven solutions from 3 unrelated fields (e.g., aviation, game design, ER medicine, ecology).
If you redesigned [Your Project/Habit] using video game design principles, which feedback loops, difficulty curves, and anti-friction mechanics would you steal?

note.zh: 把航空飞行检查单跨界移植到外科手术室，大幅降低事故率
note.en: Transplanting aviation checklists into hospital operating rooms to cut errors dramatically

title.zh: 先花 3 分钟“改写问题”，再让 AI 回答问题
title.en: Reframing the Question for 3 Minutes Before Asking AI for Answers

old_assumption.zh: 脑子里刚冒出一个模糊念头，就直接丢给 AI 要方案，拿到平庸答案再怪 AI 不够聪明。
old_assumption.en: Typing a vague half-baked thought straight into AI and blaming generic answers on the model.

new_shift.zh: 80% 的平庸回答源于模糊提问；先让 AI 帮自己暴露前提假设、拆解隐藏变量、生成 3 个不同切角的精准母题，后续产出质量会呈阶梯式跃升。
new_shift.en: Most generic AI outputs come from vague questions—spending 3 minutes surfacing hidden assumptions and sharper angles upgrades every answer that follows.

zh: 我现在的模糊想法是：[粘贴你的模糊念头]。先不要给我最终方案，请帮我找出这句话里的 3 个隐含前提，并把我的问题改写成 3 个角度完全不同的精准提问。
针对 [你最近卡住的一个难题]，请用“五问法/反事实追问”帮我确认：我真正要解决的核心矛盾到底是什么，还是只是在修枝叶？
en: My rough thought is: [Paste Rough Thought]. Before solving it, surface 3 hidden assumptions in my framing and rewrite this into 3 sharper questions from distinct angles.
For [Problem You're Stuck On], help me test whether I'm solving the real bottleneck or polishing a symptom, and suggest the sharpest question to ask next.

note.zh: 用结构化母题库把“不知道该问什么”变成可复用的探索起点
note.en: Turning 'unknown unknowns' into structured starting questions before deep AI execution

title.zh: 区分“可逆门”与“单向门”，该快的地方别慢
title.en: Separating Two-Way Doors from One-Way Doors to Move Faster

old_assumption.zh: 所有决定都要反复权衡、做足调研再行动，犹豫不决等于稳健。
old_assumption.en: Every decision deserves exhaustive analysis before acting; hesitating feels cautious and safe.

new_shift.zh: 在试错成本极低的今天，把大量“可逆小决定（Two-Way Door）”当成“不可逆大赌注”反复内耗，才是最大的隐形时间黑洞；可逆的事先跑起来再改。
new_shift.en: Over-analyzing easily reversible 'two-way door' decisions wastes massive momentum—act fast on reversible bets and reserve deep scrutiny for true one-way doors.

zh: 列出我本周正在纠结的 3 件事：[填入 3 件事]。帮我判断哪些属于“低成本可逆实验”，哪些属于“高代价不可逆决策”，并给每件可逆的事定一个 24 小时内的最小行动。
针对我担心的这个风险：[描述你的顾虑]，如果最坏情况真的发生了，修复或回滚它的实际成本到底有多大？
en: Take these 3 things I'm hesitating on: [List 3 Items]. Classify which are reversible two-way doors vs. costly one-way doors, and give a 24-hour action for the reversible ones.
For this downside risk I'm worried about—[Describe Risk]—what would it actually take to reverse or recover if it happens?

note.zh: 区分可逆与不可逆决策，是提高个人与团队推进速度的关键心智模型
note.en: Distinguishing reversible experiments from irreversible commitments keeps velocity high without recklessness

title.zh: 用“缩短反馈回路”替代单纯“拉长努力时长”
title.en: Shortening Feedback Loops Instead of Extending Effort Hours

old_assumption.zh: 一件事没起色，是因为投入的时间还不够长、还不够拼。
old_assumption.en: When progress feels slow, the fix is simply putting in more hours and grinding harder.

new_shift.zh: 反馈回路太长（比如做几个月才看到一次真实用户/结果反馈）会导致盲目偏航；把验证周期缩短到几天甚至几小时，学习速度会快好几倍。
new_shift.en: Long feedback loops cause months of blind drift—shrinking validation cycles from months to days or hours accelerates real learning far more than extra hours.

zh: 我正在推进的这件事：[描述你的目标或项目]，目前要等很久才能看到真实结果反馈。请帮我设计 3 个“把反馈回路缩短到 48 小时内”的微型验证方法。
审视我目前的 [学习/创作/做项目] 习惯，找出哪个环节的反馈延迟最高，并给出一个立刻能落地的观测指标。
en: I'm working on [Goal/Project], where real feedback currently takes too long. Design 3 ways to shrink the feedback loop to under 48 hours.
Audit my current [Learning/Building/Writing] loop—where is the slowest feedback delay, and what immediate signal can I track sooner?

signals.name: Thinking in Systems — Feedback Loops (Donella Meadows)

note.zh: 系统论核心洞察：反馈延迟与结构往往决定了系统的动态表现
note.en: Systems thinking insight: feedback delays and structure drive real-world outcomes

title.zh: 多问一层“然后呢？”，盯紧规则变化后的二阶效应
title.en: Tracing Second-Order Effects After Incentives or Tools Shift

old_assumption.zh: 看到一个新工具或新规则，只看它直接带来的眼前好处就下结论。
old_assumption.en: Judging a new tool or policy only by its immediate, first-order benefit.

new_shift.zh: 当所有人都能用同一个新手段时，激励结构和竞争生态会发生二阶变化——原本的优势可能变成新拥堵，真正的机会往往藏在下一层反应里。
new_shift.en: Once everyone adopts the same shortcut, incentives and congestion shift in second-order ways—real advantage often sits one step past the obvious effect.

zh: 针对 [某个正在普及的新工具/新规则/新趋势，如 AI 生成内容/自动化工具/某平台机制]，请帮我推演它的“一阶直接好处”以及 3 个可能出现的“二阶副作用或新机会”。
如果 [某个你打算采取的行动/习惯改变] 持续执行半年，除了预期结果之外，它可能会悄悄改变我的哪些作息、精力或人际节奏？
en: For [New Tool, Rule, or Trend], map its immediate first-order benefit plus 3 likely second-order side effects or downstream opportunities.
If I keep up [Planned Action or Habit Change] for 6 months, what second-order shifts might it trigger in my schedule, energy, or priorities?

note.zh: 二阶思维：大多数人只看第一步，看清第二步与第三步的人往往更有胜算
note.en: Second-order thinking looks past immediate effects to spot downstream reactions most people miss

title.zh: 用“最小可验证问题”给热门概念挤泡沫
title.en: Deflating Hype with One Falsifiable Question

old_assumption.zh: 某个概念被吹得很热，要么盲目追捧怕错过，要么一棍子打死觉得全是炒作。
old_assumption.en: When a buzzword is everywhere, people either jump in out of FOMO or dismiss the whole thing as hype.

new_shift.zh: 真正的区分不在“信不信”，而在“具体卡在哪”——用 1～2 个直击成本、延迟、数据或真实留存的问题，就能快速剥出真价值与真局限。
new_shift.en: Real clarity comes not from hype or cynicism, but from asking sharp questions about cost, latency, failure modes, and real retention.

zh: 最近很火的一个概念/工具是：[填入概念或工具名]。请帮我拆解：它吹嘘的理想场景是什么、目前最真实的落地卡点是什么、以及哪些场景其实用传统简单方案就够了？
给我设计一份“3 问挤泡沫清单”，以后我看到任何新名词或新方案，都能在 5 分钟内判断它值不值得我花时间深入。
en: A trending concept or tool right now is [Concept/Tool]. Break down its ideal pitch, real-world bottlenecks today, and where a simpler existing approach is already enough.
Create a 3-question hype filter I can run in 5 minutes whenever I encounter a shiny new buzzword or framework.

note.zh: 把宏大叙事拉回工程成本、维护负担与真实业务指标，是挤泡沫最有效的尺子
note.en: Checking real costs, maintenance burden, and actual metrics cuts through buzzwords fast

title.zh: 先把“默认假设”列出来，再决定要不要打破它
title.en: Listing Hidden Assumptions Before Deciding Which Ones to Challenge

old_assumption.zh: 很多前提条件是“天经地义”的，不用专门拿出来检视。
old_assumption.en: Many background premises are obvious facts of life and don't need explicit inspection.

new_shift.zh: 最大的认知盲区往往藏在“连自己都没意识到的默认假设”里；一旦把前提写到纸上，立刻就能看清哪些是铁律、哪些只是过时习惯。
new_shift.en: The biggest blindspots hide inside unexamined defaults—writing assumptions down separates real constraints from outdated habits.

zh: 针对我目前正在做的这件事：[描述你的计划或现状]，帮我列出它背后依赖的 6 条“默认假设”，并标出哪些最可能已经不再成立。
用“如果反过来会怎样”的思维，帮我挑战 [某个你一直深信不疑的行业/个人规则]，看看打破后会发生什么。
en: For my current plan or situation—[Describe Plan/Situation]—list 6 hidden assumptions it relies on and flag which ones may no longer hold.
Challenge [Rule or Convention You Take for Granted] by asking what changes if we invert it or remove the constraint.

note.zh: 剥离层层叠加的约定俗成、回到基本事实重新推理，是打破定式的核心动作
note.en: Stripping conventions back to core truths is the heart of first-principles reasoning

title.zh: 定好“何时停手”的规则，别在边际收益归零处死磕
title.en: Setting Stopping Rules Before Diminishing Returns Drain You

old_assumption.zh: 一件事没做完、没调到完美就不该停，越往后改越精细总是好的。
old_assumption.en: Keep pushing and polishing until every detail feels finished—more effort always improves the result.

new_shift.zh: 很多工作和研究在 80% 处就已经够用，后面 20% 往往边际收益极低却耗掉 80% 精力；提前设好“时间盒 / 止损线”，把省下的精力留给下一局。
new_shift.en: Past a clear threshold, extra polishing yields tiny gains at huge energy cost—clear timeboxes and stopping rules protect energy for higher-leverage bets.

zh: 我经常在 [某类任务，如查资料/改稿/调参数/挑方案] 上陷进去停不下来。请帮我设计一套“提前设定的停手规则（Stopping Rule）”，帮我及时收尾。
针对我本周的一件重要事项：[描述事项]，帮我定义“什么叫已经足够好（Good Enough to Ship）”的务实标准。
en: I tend to over-iterate and lose track of time on [Task Type, e.g., research/editing/tweaking/choosing]. Design practical stopping rules so I wrap up cleanly.
For [Important Task This Week], define a pragmatic 'good enough to ship' bar so I don't over-polish past diminishing returns.

signals.name: Algorithms to Live By — Stopping Rules

note.zh: 何时停止搜索与打磨，是日常决策中极实用却常被忽略的策略问题
note.en: Knowing when to stop searching or tweaking is a practical decision rule in everyday work

title.zh: 先看“基准率（Base Rate）”，再看吸睛的极端个案
title.en: Checking Base Rates Before Being Swayed by Outliers

old_assumption.zh: 看到一个人靠某个捷径或风口一夜翻身，就以为这件事对大多数人也是常态。
old_assumption.en: Seeing a dramatic outlier success makes it feel like a typical outcome anyone can replicate easily.

new_shift.zh: 幸存者偏差会放大极端个案；先看大样本下的真实概率、时间和投入成本，再决定要不要押注，心态会清醒很多。
new_shift.en: Outlier stories distort expectations—checking realistic base rates, timelines, and effort first keeps plans grounded without killing ambition.

zh: 我最近对 [某个方向/路径/副业/赛道] 很心动，但只看到了一些成功案例。请帮我客观分析它的“真实基准率”、常见卡点以及通常需要多久才能看到起色。
在评估 [某个目标或计划] 的时间与精力投入时，如何避免只按最顺利的“理想剧本”算账？
en: I'm drawn to [Path, Side Bet, or Goal] after seeing standout stories. Give a realistic look at base rates, common bottlenecks, and typical timelines to traction.
How can I avoid planning around a 'best-case script' when estimating time and effort for [Goal or Project]?

note.zh: 参考类预测用同类历史经验校准乐观偏差，让计划更贴近现实
note.en: Reference-class forecasting calibrates optimism bias using comparable real-world outcomes

title.zh: 把“客观事实”和“脑补故事”分开写，卡壳瞬间解开
title.en: Separating Hard Facts from the Stories Your Brain Invents

old_assumption.zh: 遇到挫折、误会或卡壳时，脑子里的猜测和情绪往往被当成了既成事实。
old_assumption.en: When things go sideways or stall, anxious interpretations and worst-case guesses feel like objective facts.

new_shift.zh: 把事件拆成两栏——“纯客观发生的事” vs “我自己推演/脑补的故事”——很多内耗和误判会当场缩小一半。
new_shift.en: Splitting a situation into 'verifiable facts' vs. 'stories and assumptions I'm adding' cuts through emotional fog and reveals what can actually be tested.

zh: 我现在因为 [某件事/某段沟通/某个进度卡点] 觉得有点堵或烦躁：[简述情况]。请帮我把“客观事实”和“我的主观猜测/担心”拆开列出来，并给出下一步最务实的验证动作。
针对 [某个让你纠结的判断]，哪些是已经有证据支撑的，哪些只是惯性联想？
en: I feel stuck or tense about [Situation, Message, or Bottleneck]: [Brief Context]. Separate verifiable facts from my assumptions/worries, and suggest one practical next check.
For [Judgment I'm Mulling Over], which parts have concrete evidence vs. habit-driven assumptions?

note.zh: 觉察自己从事实跳到结论的推理阶梯，是减少误解与情绪内耗的实用工具
note.en: Noticing how fast we jump from raw facts to interpretations reduces friction and overthinking

title.zh: 先找到“真正的唯一瓶颈”，别在非瓶颈环节拼命卷
title.en: Finding the Real Bottleneck Before Optimizing Everything Else

old_assumption.zh: 每个环节都一起优化、一起加把劲，整体效率就会跟着全面提升。
old_assumption.en: Improving every step or working harder across the board lifts overall throughput evenly.

new_shift.zh: 整条链路的上限往往卡在最窄的那一环；在瓶颈没解开前，给其他环节加再多马力也只是堆积半成品或浪费精力。
new_shift.en: A pipeline's output is capped by its tightest constraint—pushing non-bottleneck steps before clearing the real bottleneck creates pileups and wasted effort.

zh: 我推进 [某个项目/工作流/学习或创作目标] 时感觉整体卡住了：[简述各环节现状]。请帮我诊断：目前真正的“最窄瓶颈”卡在哪一步？优先该先动哪一刀？
在 [你的日常工作流] 中，哪些看起来很忙但其实不在主瓶颈上的动作，可以先放一放？
en: Progress on [Project, Workflow, or Goal] feels stuck: [Describe Steps & Current State]. Help me pinpoint the tightest bottleneck and the single highest-leverage fix.
In [Your Workflow], which busy-looking tasks sit off the main bottleneck and can wait until the core constraint is resolved?

note.zh: 约束理论：集中精力突破系统中的关键限制，往往比均匀用力更有效
note.en: Focusing improvement effort on the system's key constraint beats spreading effort evenly

title.zh: 只看“接下来投入什么、换来什么”，别被过去的沉没成本绑架
title.en: Deciding From Future Trade-Offs Instead of Past Sunk Costs

old_assumption.zh: 已经花了好几个月、好几千块或很多心血了，现在停下来或改方向就等于全盘亏光。
old_assumption.en: Having already sunk months, money, or effort into something means stopping or pivoting wastes everything you put in.

new_shift.zh: 过去花掉的时间和钱已经回不来了，继续硬撑只会多搭进未来的时间与机会；换个视角问自己：“如果今天才刚知道这件事，我还愿意从头选它吗？”
new_shift.en: Past costs are already gone—clinging to them taxes your future time and options. Ask: knowing what I know today, would I choose to start this fresh?

zh: 我目前在 [某个项目/方向/订阅或投入] 上已经花了较多时间或精力，但隐约觉得不对劲：[简述情况]。请帮我抽离沉没成本，客观评估“继续推进 vs 调整/停手”的未来得失。
帮我写 3 个犀利的问题，以后当我因为“舍不得前面投入”而犹豫是否转向时，能帮我冷静看清真实处境。
en: I've already put significant time or effort into [Project, Path, or Commitment], but it feels off: [Brief Context]. Evaluate continuing vs. pivoting based purely on future costs and upside.
Give me 3 clear questions to cut through sunk-cost attachment when deciding whether to keep going or change course.

note.zh: 识别沉没成本偏误，能帮助人在方向不对时更早释放注意力与时间
note.en: Spotting sunk-cost bias frees time and attention earlier when a path stops paying off

title.zh: 刻意找“能推翻自己看法的证据”，而不只搜集赞同理由
title.en: Actively Looking for Disconfirming Evidence Over Echoes

old_assumption.zh: 看准了一件事后，找更多支持自己的案例和观点，心里就更有底了。
old_assumption.en: Once you lean toward an idea or judgment, gathering supporting examples confirms you're on track.

new_shift.zh: 确认偏误会让人只看到想看的东西；主动问“什么情况下我的判断会错、有哪些反例”，才能在押注前看清盲区。
new_shift.en: Confirmation bias filters out warning signs—asking what would prove you wrong and seeking counter-examples exposes blindspots before you overcommit.

zh: 我目前倾向于认为：[填入你的看法或计划]。请帮我列出 4 个可能推翻或削弱这个看法的反例、潜在风险或反面视角。
如果我要验证 [某个重要假设] 到底靠不靠谱，最值得优先去查的 2 个反面证据是什么？
en: I currently lean toward [Your View or Plan]. Give me 4 counter-examples, risks, or alternative angles that could challenge or falsify it.
To test whether [Key Assumption] holds up in reality, what 2 disconfirming checks should I run first?

note.zh: 主动寻找反证是校准判断、避免陷入自我印证闭环的关键心智习惯
note.en: Seeking disconfirming evidence helps calibrate judgment before conviction outruns reality

title.zh: 信息永远不可能 100% 齐备，在“够用信息”下做决定
title.en: Deciding With 'Good Enough' Information Instead of Waiting for 100% Certainty

old_assumption.zh: 等把所有资料都看完、所有变量都算准了，再做决定才算负责任。
old_assumption.en: Wait until every fact is gathered and every uncertainty is resolved before making a call.

new_shift.zh: 现实中绝大多数决定都要在信息不完全时做出；等太久往往错过窗口或白耗精力，看清关键变量与底线后果后果断拍板更务实。
new_shift.en: Most real decisions happen under incomplete info—waiting for 100% certainty often costs time and options, whereas acting on key trade-offs and downside limits keeps moving.

zh: 我在 [某个决定/选择] 上一直等“再多看点资料再定”：[简述纠结点]。请帮我列出做这个决定真正关键的 3 个变量，以及我现在其实已经足够判断的依据。
针对 [当前纠结的选择]，帮我对比“现在就定并边走边调”与“再等两周调研”各自的机会成本。
en: I keep holding off on [Decision or Choice] to gather more info: [Brief Context]. Identify the 3 variables that actually matter and what I already know enough to judge.
Compare deciding now and adjusting as we go vs. waiting two more weeks to research [Decision]—what is the real trade-off?

note.zh: 聚焦关键变量与可承受代价，能帮助人在不完美信息下保持行动力
note.en: Focusing on decisive variables and tolerable downside keeps action moving when info is incomplete

title.zh: 揪出你从未签字、却一直在履行的“隐性合约”
title.en: Surfacing Implicit Contracts You Never Signed Yet Keep Honoring

old_assumption.zh: 很多做事规矩和人生步骤既然大家都在照做，说明那是客观条件或默认必选项。
old_assumption.en: When everyone follows a norm or milestone sequence, it feels like an objective constraint rather than a choice.

new_shift.zh: 许多卡点来自你顺手接受的“未签字合约”（比如做工具必须通用、产出必须公开发布、遇到问题先找现成方案）；一旦挑明，很多束缚当场失效。
new_shift.en: Much friction comes from unsigned contracts you treat as binding—naming them lets you renegotiate or drop rules that never served your real goal.

zh: 审视我目前正在推进的 [项目/工作流/生活安排]：[简述现状]。帮我列出 4 条我可能“默认签了字、但其实根本没必要遵守”的隐性合约，并指出哪一条最值得立刻打破。
针对 [某个让你觉得被绑住或有负担的规矩或惯例]，帮我拆解：这是真实硬约束，还是只是习惯成自然的隐性预设？
en: Audit my current [Project, Workflow, or Routine]: [Brief Context]. Surface 4 implicit 'contracts' I may be honoring by default without ever agreeing to them, and flag the easiest one to break.
For [Rule or Habit That Feels Restrictive], separate real external constraints from unexamined habits we can rewrite.

note.zh: 把看似既定的前提拆开检视，往往能发现根本不存在的隐形围栏
note.en: Inspecting taken-for-granted premises reveals invisible fences you never had to stay inside

title.zh: 别在“算错坐标系的题”上算得更准，先换题目坐标系
title.en: Stop Computing Faster Inside the Wrong Problem Coordinate System

old_assumption.zh: 推进不顺或结果不理想时，说明方法还不够细、执行还不够到位。
old_assumption.en: When a plan stalls or misses, the fix is sharper execution or more detail inside the same framing.

new_shift.zh: 有时问题卡住不是算力不够，而是“题目本身问在错误的坐标系里”（比如用线性时间去解非线性跃迁，或用局部指标代替真实结果）；换坐标系比加倍努力更有效。
new_shift.en: Stalling often means you're optimizing inside the wrong frame—shifting the problem's coordinates or unit of measure unlocks leverage that extra effort cannot.

zh: 我最近在 [某个目标/项目/难题] 上花了不少力气但进展有限：[简述现状]。请帮我跳出当前解法，提出 2 个完全不同的“问题坐标系”来重新定义这件事。
检查我目前用来衡量 [某件事进展] 的指标：[填当前指标]，它有没有可能把人引向错误方向？建议一个更贴近本质的替代视角。
en: I've put real effort into [Goal, Project, or Problem] with limited traction: [Brief Context]. Step outside current fixes and propose 2 different coordinate frames to re-pose the problem.
Check the metric I use for [Project or Habit]—[Current Metric]—and tell me how it could distort behavior or miss what actually matters.

note.zh: 切换观察问题的坐标系，常能把死结变成顺手可解的题
note.en: Changing the coordinate frame often turns a stubborn dead-end into a clean question

title.zh: 从“技能执行者”转向“问题定义与验收者”
title.en: Shifting from Executor to Specifier & Quality Reviewer

old_assumption.zh: 个人职业护城河取决于自己亲手把活干得多快、工具用得多熟练。
old_assumption.en: Career moat depends on how fast and skillfully you execute tasks by hand.

new_shift.zh: 纯执行正在被 AI 快速廉价化，真正稀缺且高薪的能力正迅速向两端集中：精准写清需求规格（Spec）与一眼揪出隐蔽缺陷（Review）。
new_shift.en: Pure execution is rapidly commoditizing; high-value leverage now concentrates at two ends—writing razor-sharp specs and spotting subtle defects in AI output.

zh: 针对 [你的职业/岗位]，列出 5 个正在被 AI 迅速贬值的纯执行技能，以及 5 个因此变得更值钱的“定义问题/质量验收/责任兜底”类高杠杆能力。
帮我为 [你日常交付的一类核心产出，如 PRD/代码/营销方案] 设计一份“资深专家级验收清单（Review Rubric）”，让我从自己埋头写变成高效把关。
en: For [Your Role], list 5 pure execution skills rapidly losing market value to AI, and 5 high-leverage 'problem framing, taste, and quality review' skills rising in value.
Create a senior-level Review Rubric for [Core Deliverable You Produce] so I can shift from manual drafting to high-leverage specification and quality control.

note.zh: 工程界正从“手写每行代码”转向“维护高精度规格说明书与自动化测试”
note.en: Software engineering shifting from hand-coding toward high-precision specs and verification

title.zh: 用“2+1 技能组合”构造微型个人垄断
title.en: Building a Personal Micro-Monopoly via Skill Stacking

old_assumption.zh: 要在职场上胜出，必须在某一个单一赛道卷到全球前 1%。
old_assumption.en: To win in your career, you must grind into the top 1% of a single crowded discipline.

new_shift.zh: 单一维度卷前 1% 极难，但把两项前 20% 的常见技能加上一个独特行业语境交叉叠加，就能立刻在交叉点形成几乎没有竞争对手的微型垄断。
new_shift.en: Reaching top 1% in one skill is brutal—combining two top-20% skills with one specific domain context creates an almost competition-free micro-monopoly.

zh: 我目前具备的技能、经历和兴趣包括：[列出 3-5 个你的标签]。请帮我做交叉组合，找出 5 个我不需要和顶级专家硬碰硬、却能天然占据优势的“微型生态位”。
在我现有的核心能力 [技能 A] 之外，只需花 3 个月补齐哪一个“低门槛跨界技能 [技能 B]”，就能让我的稀缺度和议价能力翻倍？
en: My current skills, experiences, and interests are: [List 3-5 Traits]. Cross-combine them to identify 5 micro-monopoly niches where I have an unfair edge without fighting top-1% specialists.
Beside my core skill [Skill A], which adjacent skill could I learn to a solid top-20% level in 90 days to double my rarity and leverage?

note.zh: 经典“技能栈”模型：用多项前 25% 能力的组合击败单一维度的内卷
note.en: Classic talent-stack concept: combining multiple top-25% skills beats single-track grinding

title.zh: 用“前置作品证明”替代投递千篇一律的简历
title.en: Replacing Generic Resumes with Permissionless Proof-of-Work

old_assumption.zh: 找好机会、好客户或好工作，必须把简历投进招聘网站排队等 HR 筛选。
old_assumption.en: Landing great roles or clients means submitting a PDF resume into job portals and waiting.

new_shift.zh: AI 让投递成本归零后，HR 和甲方被海量完美简历淹没；直接针对目标团队的真实痛点做一个 2 小时的开源诊断或微型原型发过去，响应率高出一个数量级。
new_shift.en: AI flooded job boards with identical resumes—sending a 2-hour permissionless teardown or working mini-prototype for a target team's real problem cuts straight through the noise.

zh: 我想争取 [目标公司/目标客户类型] 的合作或岗位机会，我的强项是 [你的专长]。请帮我设计一个只需花半天时间就能做出的“免许可前置作品（Permissionless Proof-of-Work）”，以及一封 100 字以内不卑不亢的触达邮件。
把我的这段普通工作经历：[粘贴一段简历描述]，改造成一个让陌生人点开链接 30 秒就能看懂我实力的“可验证公开案例”。
